categories.label: The therapist's licensing board
categories.blurb: Holds the individual clinician's licence and can suspend or revoke it.

categories.label: The agency that licenses the program
categories.blurb: Inspects the facility itself and can cite, fine, suspend or close it.

categories.label: Law enforcement and legal channels
categories.blurb: Child protection, the Attorney General, and the criminal side.

categories.label: Oversight and advocacy
categories.blurb: Bodies with a right to investigate, and advocates who can act for you.

national.note: Bodies that take a report wherever the program is. None of these replaces the state channels: the state licensing board and the state licensor are the ones that can take somebody's licence away. For crisis lines, see the Resources page - this list is about reporting, not about getting through tonight.

deadlines.text: Deadlines for abuse of a child usually run from the survivor's 18th birthday, or from when they came to understand what happened, not from the day the program closed. Many states have lengthened them, removed them for child sexual abuse, or reopened claims that had already expired. A criminal charge, a lawsuit and a licence complaint each have their own deadline, so one having passed does not mean the others have.
deadlines.link_label: CHILD USA's statute of limitations tracker, updated as each state changes its law

channels.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: Talks through what happened, tells you which state agency takes the report, and stays on the line while you work out what to say. Counselors are available 24/7.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It is not itself an investigating agency. It routes you; it does not open a case.
channels.who_to_report: Anyone unsure where a report about a child should go, including a survivor who is now an adult and a parent who has just got their child out.
channels.how: Call, text GO to the same number, or use the live chat on the site.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours, every day. Text GO to 800-422-4453, or chat from the website.

channels.name: State child abuse and neglect reporting numbers (Child Welfare Information Gateway)
channels.what_it_can_do: The federal government's directory of every state's child protection intake line, with each state's online reporting option where one exists.
channels.who_to_report: A child currently at the program. Report to the state the program sits in, not the state the family lives in - the agency with jurisdiction is the one where the child is.
channels.how: Find the state on the directory page, then call that state's intake line.
channels.note: Most states take an anonymous report but will act on more of it if they can call you back.

channels.name: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes reports of civil rights violations, including conditions in institutions where people are held. Its Special Litigation Section is the part that investigates residential facilities under CRIPA and can sue an institution or a state over a pattern of abuse.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It does not act for one person against one program. It looks for patterns, and it decides on its own whether to open anything.
channels.who_to_report: A facility where the abuse is systemic rather than one member of staff - restraint practice, seclusion, denial of medical care, conditions across a whole program.
channels.how: Submit the online report form. Paper forms can be downloaded and mailed.
channels.mail: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division, 950 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20530-0001

channels.name: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates fraud and abuse in federally funded health programs. Where a program bills Medicaid, this is often the lever that moves first, because billing for treatment that was not given is easier to prove than the treatment being abusive.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It will not get you a refund or a remedy in your own case, and says so plainly. Volume means most complaints get no reply.
channels.who_to_report: A program billing Medicaid or another federal program - for therapy hours nobody delivered, for staff who were not qualified, for a level of care the child was not getting.
channels.how: Submit through the online tips portal. It only takes unclassified complaints online.

channels.name: Your state's Protection and Advocacy agency
channels.what_it_can_do: Every state has one, funded by Congress. Under the DD Act and PAIMI they have legal authority to investigate abuse and neglect wherever a person with a disability receives services, and a right of access to the place itself - they can go in. Several of the hardest reports on programs in this industry came from P&A investigations.
channels.who_to_report: A program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis, which covers most placements in this industry. You do not need a formal diagnosis to call and ask.
channels.how: Find your state's agency in the NDRN directory and contact its intake line. Report to the state the program is in.

channels.name: The Joint Commission, Office of Quality and Patient Safety
channels.what_it_can_do: Accredits behavioral health organisations and can review, cite, or ultimately withdraw accreditation. Losing accreditation can cost a program its insurance contracts and its Medicaid participation, which is sometimes the fastest real consequence available.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It only has standing over organisations it accredits, and it does not discipline an individual clinician. Check the program is accredited first.
channels.who_to_report: A Joint Commission accredited facility. Its Find Accredited Organizations search will tell you whether a program is one.
channels.how: Use the online submission form, which it prefers, or call. It does not take walk-ins, faxes or email, and it shreds medical records, photos and invoices on arrival.
channels.mail: Office of Quality and Patient Safety, The Joint Commission, One Renaissance Boulevard, Oakbrook Terrace, IL 60181
channels.note: You can file anonymously, but it can only tell you what it did with the complaint if you give your name.

channels.name: CARF International
channels.what_it_can_do: The other accreditor much of this industry uses. Takes concerns about an accredited provider and can act on its accreditation.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: Like any accreditor it has no power over an unaccredited program, and none over an individual therapist's licence.
channels.who_to_report: A CARF-accredited program. CARF asks you to try the provider's own grievance process first, and says to go to your state P&A agency or the state licensor if that does not resolve it.
channels.how: Use the feedback form on the public page, or call the dedicated line.
channels.mail: CARF International, 6951 East Southpoint Road, Tucson, AZ 85756

states.note: Alabama reports child abuse to the county Department of Human Resources or to local law enforcement rather than to a single state hotline, and the county has seven calendar days to begin investigating - immediately where there is immediate danger to health or safety. Complaints about a facility go somewhere else again, to the Child Care Services Division intake line.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Assault, battery and false imprisonment: six years. Negligence and other personal-injury claims: two years. A claim that holds an employer (such as a program) responsible for what its staff did, under respondeat superior, must be brought within two years.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: In Alabama you are a minor until 19. Someone hurt before 19 has until three years after their 19th birthday (age 22), or less if the normal deadline is shorter: for a two-year claim like negligence, until age 21. No claim can be extended more than 20 years past the injury.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Claims against the State itself go to the State Board of Adjustment within one year (the State cannot be sued in court); tort claims against a city must be filed with the city clerk within six months; claims against a county must be presented within 12 months (a minor has 12 months after turning 19).

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Willful abuse, cruel beating or torture of a child under 18 is a felony. If it involved violence, attempted violence, a threat of violence or serious physical injury, there is no time limit to prosecute. Otherwise, five years from the offense.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault involves violence, so there is no time limit to prosecute it. Other felonies: five years. Misdemeanor assault: 12 months.

channels.name: Alabama Board of Examiners in Counseling
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and certifies counselors in private practice in Alabama and disciplines unethical practice by licensed professional counselors.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor in Alabama. The Board publishes a licensee search so you can confirm the licence first.
channels.how: Use the Board's fillable complaint form, which it publishes alongside separate written instructions for filling it in.
channels.mail: Alabama Board of Examiners in Counseling, 400 South Union Street, Suite 245, Montgomery, AL 36104

channels.name: Alabama Board of Examiners in Psychology
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in Alabama.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist.
channels.how: Use the Board's complaints page.

channels.name: Alabama DHR, Child Care Services Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child care and residential providers against Alabama's Child Care Minimum Standards and investigates complaints that a provider has breached them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed provider - conditions, staffing, supervision, anything that breaches the minimum standards.
channels.how: Call the intake line and ask for Child Care Intake, or email the licensing intake address.

channels.name: Alabama child abuse and neglect reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a county Department of Human Resources or law enforcement investigation. The county or the law enforcement authority must investigate within seven calendar days of the report, and immediately where there is immediate danger to a child's health or safety.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Alabama program. Report to the county DHR office where the program is, or to local law enforcement there.
channels.how: Call the county DHR office, local law enforcement, or the state line.
channels.phone_note: For reporting suspected child abuse anywhere in Alabama.

channels.name: Alabama Disabilities Advocacy Program (ADAP)
channels.what_it_can_do: Alabama's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy. It publishes its own guide to abuse and neglect of people with disabilities.
channels.who_to_report: An Alabama program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against all defendants is age 25 when the victim is under age 19.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for felony and misdemeanor sex offenses. There is an SOL of five years from the offense for other felonies and one year for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking offenses against victims under age 16, and for victims ages 16 and 17 the SOL is age twenty-four.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM offenses against victims under age 16, and for victims ages 16 and 17 the SOL is age twenty-four.

states.note: Alaska takes abuse reports by phone, email or fax, and says its hotline staff will answer questions about mandatory reporting and take all the required information over the phone - which is worth knowing if you are unsure whether what you have is enough to report. All the mental health licensing boards sit under one division, with a single investigations unit behind them.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from when the injury happened (when the claim 'accrued'). The same two years covers assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence/personal injury.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18, but the extension cannot go more than two years past the 18th birthday. In practice, someone hurt as a minor has until age 20.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: No advance notice of claim is required to sue the State of Alaska in tort; the normal two-year deadline applies. But the State cannot be sued for claims arising out of assault, battery or false imprisonment (only negligence-type claims), so a survivor may need to sue the individual staff or a private contractor instead.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Alaska has no separate felony 'physical child abuse' crime; physical abuse of a child is charged as assault (including third-degree assault for injuring a child under 12, or 12-15). Felony assault must be charged within 10 years of the offense. The clock is not paused until the child turns 18 for these non-sexual crimes.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault (first, second or third degree) must be charged within 10 years of the offense. Misdemeanor assault and other offenses: five years.

channels.name: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Staffs and investigates for the Board of Professional Counselors, the Board of Psychologist and Psychological Associate Examiners and the Board of Social Work Examiners, and the boards discipline the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor, psychologist, psychological associate or social worker in Alaska.
channels.how: File the complaint with the Division, which handles investigations for all three boards.
channels.mail: Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing, 550 W 7th Ave, Ste 1500, Anchorage, AK 99501-3567

channels.name: Alaska Office of Children's Services reporting hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect in Alaska.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Alaska program.
channels.how: Call, email or fax. Staff will answer questions about mandatory reporting and take everything they need over the phone.
channels.note: If the problem is the Office of Children's Services itself rather than a program, there is a separate formal complaint process for that.

channels.name: Alaska residential child care facility licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses Alaska's residential child care facilities against the state licensing regulations and investigates complaints that a facility has breached them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Alaska residential child care facility.
channels.how: Start from the Department's reporting hub, which sets out which body takes which kind of concern.
channels.phone_note: The Office of Children's Services line also takes concerns about licensed facilities.

channels.name: Disability Law Center of Alaska
channels.what_it_can_do: Alaska's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Alaska program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no civil SOL for sexual abuse or assault claims against perpetrators. The SOL is age 21 or 3 years from discovery for some other CSA claims against perpetrators, and the SOL is age 20 or 2 years from discovery for the remaining CSA claims against all defendants.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking claims against perpetrators.
CSAM: There is no SOL for unlawful exploitation of a minor claims against perpetrators.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for many CSA crimes. The SOL for remaining felonies and misdemeanors is 5 years from the offense.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for felony sex trafficking violations when the victim is under age 20.
CSAM: There is no SOL for unlawful exploitation of a minor or distribution of child pornography.

states.note: Arizona splits the work three ways: the Board of Behavioral Health Examiners holds the therapist's licence, the Department of Health Services licenses the behavioral health residential facility, and the Department of Child Safety runs both the abuse hotline and its own Office of Licensing and Regulation for group homes. Which licensor applies depends on how the program is registered, so the DHS facility database is worth checking first.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for physical injuries, including assault, battery and negligence. False imprisonment (for example, being held against your will) has a shorter deadline: one year.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18. After turning 18 they get the full normal period: two years for injury claims (until age 20), one year for false imprisonment.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Before suing a state or local government body, public school or public employee, you must file a written notice of claim, with a specific settlement amount, within 180 days; the lawsuit itself must be filed within one year. A minor may file the notice within 180 days after turning 18.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony child abuse must be charged within seven years after the state discovers (or reasonably should have discovered) the offense. There is no rule pausing it until the child turns 18, but the clock starts at discovery, not the act.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Aggravated assault and other class 2-6 felonies: seven years from when the state discovers the offense. Misdemeanor assault: one year.

channels.name: Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses social workers, counselors, marriage and family therapists and substance abuse counselors, investigates complaints against them and disciplines those who breach the standards of practice or their profession's code of ethics.
channels.who_to_report: Any of those four licence types. Psychologists are licensed separately by the Arizona Board of Psychologist Examiners, and physicians by the Arizona Medical Board.
channels.how: File through the Board's online complaint portal, or post the complaint to the Phoenix address.
channels.mail: Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners, 1740 W. Adams St., Suite 3600, Phoenix, AZ 85007
channels.note: The Board's own site sits behind a filter that refuses automated clients, so it may look unreachable to a link checker while loading normally in a browser.

channels.name: Arizona Department of Health Services, Behavioral Health Facilities Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and inspects behavioral health residential facilities, and investigates complaints about them. It publishes a licence history search and a map of every licensed facility, along with professional licence revocations.
channels.who_to_report: The facility. Check the AZ Care Check licence history first - it shows what a program has already been cited for.
channels.how: Use the online complaint form.

channels.name: Arizona Child Abuse Hotline (Department of Child Safety)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect. Reports are taken by a social work professional, and where the child is in a licensed facility the hotline also forwards the report to whichever body holds that licence.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Arizona program. Arizona law (ARS 13-3620.A) requires certain people who suspect non-accidental injury or neglect to report it to DCS or to law enforcement.
channels.how: Call the statewide toll-free hotline, or report to a local law enforcement office. Have the child's details, where they are now, and what your concern is.
channels.note: DCS finishes by marking a report substantiated or unsubstantiated. Unsubstantiated means the information gathered did not support a finding, not that nothing happened.

channels.name: Arizona DCS Office of Licensing and Regulation
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates the group homes and child welfare agencies that DCS oversees, as distinct from the behavioral health facilities DHS licenses.
channels.who_to_report: A group home or child welfare agency rather than a licensed behavioral health residential facility.
channels.how: Contact the office through DCS. DCS also runs a separate ombudsman complaint form for disagreements with the department itself.

channels.name: Disability Rights Arizona
channels.what_it_can_do: Arizona's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Arizona program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

channels.name: Arizona Ombudsman-Citizens' Aide
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office that investigates complaints about state agencies, including the Department of Child Safety. The route to take when the state body you reported to has not acted.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It looks at the agency's conduct, not the program's. It cannot licence, fine or prosecute anybody.
channels.who_to_report: Somebody who has already reported to an Arizona agency and got nowhere.

civil: CSA: The civil SOL for CSA claims against all defendants is age 30 with a common law discovery rule.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for claims of sex trafficking against all defendants.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM claims is age 20.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for many felony CSA crimes. The SOL for all other felonies is 7 years after the State discovers the offense and 1 year after the State’s discovery for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for child sex trafficking.
CSAM: There is no SOL for sexual exploitation of a minor or commercial sexual exploitation of a minor.

states.note: Two things set Arkansas apart. Its child abuse hotline is run by the State Police Crimes Against Children Division rather than by the human services department, so a report there goes straight to law enforcement. And the Office of Long-Term Care - the sole licensing authority for Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities - now publishes its monitoring reports, complaint visit reports, corrective action plans and notices of adverse action online, so you can read a facility's record before you call.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Assault, battery and false imprisonment: only one year from the injury. Negligence claims (for example, against a program for failing to protect you) are generally three years.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Someone injured as a minor gets three years after reaching adulthood to sue, whatever the normal deadline (so even the one-year battery claim becomes three years after turning 18).

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Claims against the State of Arkansas cannot go to court; they are filed with the State Claims Commission within the same deadline as a similar lawsuit. Counties, cities, school districts and other local bodies are immune from tort suits except up to their liability insurance.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony endangering the welfare of a minor and permitting abuse of a minor can be charged until the victim turns 28 if the crime was never reported to police or a prosecutor. First- and second-degree battery against a child can be charged within the normal felony period (usually three years) counted from the victim's 18th birthday, again if never reported.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Most felony assaults and batteries (Class B, C or D) must be charged within three years; Class Y or A felonies within six years. Misdemeanor assault or battery: one year. If the victim was a child and it was never reported, the period restarts at 18 (see child abuse).

channels.name: Arkansas Board of Examiners in Counseling and Marriage and Family Therapy
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints against its licensees and applicants from any person, investigates them and disciplines licences.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor or marriage and family therapist in Arkansas.
channels.how: Complaints must be in writing and on the Board's own complaint form, which is filed through its online portal.
channels.mail: Arkansas Board of Examiners in Counseling, Freeway Medical Center, 5800 W. 10th Street, Suite 405, Little Rock, AR 72204

channels.name: Arkansas Psychology Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints about the practice of any of its licensees, from any concerned citizen or organisation, and disciplines licences.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist in Arkansas.
channels.how: The complaint must be in writing, and the document has to be signed and dated. It goes to the Board's Complaints Committee.
channels.mail: Arkansas Psychology Board, Complaints Committee, 101 East Capitol, Suite 415, Little Rock, AR 72201

channels.name: Arkansas Social Work Licensing Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers in Arkansas.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed social worker.
channels.how: Contact the Board for its complaint form.

channels.name: Arkansas Office of Long-Term Care (Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities)
channels.what_it_can_do: The sole licensing authority for Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities in Arkansas. It licenses, surveys, regulates and investigates them, and takes enforcement action against failed facility practices.
channels.who_to_report: A PRTF - the licensed psychiatric residential category most Arkansas programs in this industry fall under.
channels.how: Call the complaint hotline or email the complaints address.
channels.note: Arkansas publishes PRTF monitoring and complaint visit reports, corrective action plans and notices of adverse action online. Read what has already been found against a program before you file.

channels.name: Arkansas Child Abuse Hotline (State Police Crimes Against Children Division)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child maltreatment, run by the Arkansas State Police rather than by the human services department, so a report reaches law enforcement directly.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Arkansas program. Anyone may report, at any hour.
channels.how: Call. Have the child's name and address, the alleged offender's name and address, and what happened. If a child's life may be in immediate danger, call 911 or local law enforcement first, then the hotline. Mandated reporters can file through the secure online portal instead.
channels.phone_note: Also 1-844-SAVE-A-CHILD. 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Disability Rights Arkansas
channels.what_it_can_do: Arkansas's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Arkansas program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no SOL for CSA civil claims, an open revival window for expired claims, and a 3-year discovery rule.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for some trafficking offenses and other trafficking offenses have an SOL of age 21.
CSAM: There is no SOL for some CSAM violations and other CSAM offenses have an SOL of age 21.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for some CSA crimes, including but not limited to felony rape, sex assault, incest, and exploitation. Other CSA felonies and misdemeanors have an SOL of age 28. Any remaining felonies have an SOL of six years from the offense or one year for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: The SOL for felony trafficking is 6 years from the offense. The SOL for trafficking misdemeanors is 1 year from the offense.

CSAM: There is no SOL for engaging children in sexually explicit conduct for use in a visual or print medium or for computer exploitation of a child in the first degree. The SOL for other computer child pornography violations is age 28.

states.note: California has a trap that catches families constantly. The Board of Behavioral Sciences warns that a complaint filed by anyone other than the client may be impossible to pursue, because the client owns the confidentiality of their own treatment records - so a parent complaining about their adult child's therapist, or a sibling complaining for a survivor, may need signed authorisations from everyone involved before the Board can investigate at all. Sort that out before you file, not after.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for assault, battery, and injuries caused by someone's wrongful act or negligence. False imprisonment (being held against your will) has only one year.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18, so a two-year claim can be filed until age 20 (one-year false imprisonment claims until 19). This pause does NOT apply to claims against a government body or public employee.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: For a state- or county-run facility, a written government claim must be filed within six months of the injury, and a lawsuit within six months after the claim is rejected in writing (two years if no written rejection is sent). Being a minor does not pause these deadlines, but it is grounds for the agency to accept a late claim if applied for within a year.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony child abuse or endangerment (Penal Code 273a(a)) and felony cruel corporal punishment or traumatic injury to a child (273d) must be charged within three years of the offense. The clock is not paused until the child turns 18 for these physical-abuse crimes.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault such as assault with a deadly weapon or force likely to cause great bodily injury: three years from the offense. Felonies carrying eight years or more: six years. Misdemeanor assault or battery: one year.

channels.name: California Board of Behavioral Sciences
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines marriage and family therapists, clinical social workers, professional clinical counselors and educational psychologists, and registers their associates. It can file a formal Accusation leading to probation, suspension or revocation of a licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: A third-party complaint may be impossible for it to pursue unless everyone involved authorises release of the treatment records. An anonymous complaint will be reviewed but, in the Board's own words, may be impossible to pursue without documented evidence.
channels.who_to_report: An LMFT, LCSW, LPCC or LEP, or one of their registered associates. Psychologists are the separate Board of Psychology.
channels.how: File online through DCA BreEZe, or post the Consumer Complaint Form and Authorization Release. It must be in writing, and first-hand, verifiable detail counts for much more than anything else, including contact details for anyone who can corroborate it.
channels.note: The Board says it reviews every complaint whatever its source, acknowledges receipt in writing where it can, and writes to you again if the disposition changes.

channels.name: California Community Care Licensing Division, Centralized Complaint and Information Bureau
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and inspects Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Programs, group homes and the other children's residential facilities, investigates complaints, and publishes what it finds against each facility.
channels.who_to_report: The facility. The Community Care Facility search lets you look a program up first and read its licensing record.
channels.how: Call the hotline, or complain online, by email, letter or fax.
channels.mail: California Department of Social Services, Centralized Complaint and Information Bureau, 744 P Street, Mail Station 9-3-52, Sacramento, CA 95814
channels.note: The Division says you may remain anonymous.

channels.name: Your county Child Protective Services hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: California has no statewide child abuse hotline. Each county runs its own 24-hour line, staffed by trained social workers, and that county agency investigates.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a California program. Report to the county the program sits in, not the county you live in.
channels.how: Find the county's hotline through the state's reporting page and call it. In an emergency, 911.
channels.note: If it is the county child welfare agency itself that has mishandled things, the state takes complaints about county agencies separately.

channels.name: Disability Rights California
channels.what_it_can_do: California's Protection and Advocacy agency and the largest in the country. Federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A California program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no SOL for civil CSA claims against all defendants.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking offenses is age 28.
CSAM: There is no SOL for some CSAM offenses, and an SOL of age 40 for others, with a 10-year discovery rule.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for many felony sex offenses, including rape. The SOL is age 40 for other felonies, and 1-3 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking using force, fraud, or coercion. The SOL for other trafficking violations is 6 years from the offense.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM is 10 years from the offense.

states.note: Colorado puts every licensed profession behind one complaint form at the Division of Professions and Occupations. It also has an independent Child Protection Ombudsman with its own complaint form, which publishes investigative reports naming what it found; that is a real route when a report has already been made and nothing moved.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Assault, battery and false imprisonment: one year. Negligence and most other injury claims (including outrageous conduct / emotional distress): two years. By statute, the clock starts when you knew, or reasonably should have known, both the injury and its cause.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For a minor with no court-appointed guardian, the deadline does not run until 18; they then have the normal period or two years after turning 18, whichever ends later. If a court appointed a guardian or conservator for the child, the clock runs during childhood as for an adult (the guardian gets at least two years after appointment). A parent is not a 'legal representative' unless appointed by a court.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Before suing a state or local government body or its employee, you must file a written notice within 182 days after discovering the injury (with the Attorney General for the state), then wait for a denial or 90 days; the suit itself must meet the normal deadline. Government bodies are immune except in listed situations.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony child abuse must be charged within three years of the offense, the general felony period. There is no rule pausing it until the child turns 18 for physical (non-sexual) abuse.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault must be charged within three years of the offense. Misdemeanor assault: 18 months.

channels.name: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations (DORA)
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes and investigates complaints against every mental health licence Colorado issues - psychologists, clinical social workers, professional counselors, marriage and family therapists and addiction counselors - through one form, and the boards discipline the licence.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed mental health professional in Colorado. Anyone can file: a client, a colleague, a family member.
channels.how: Use the Division's single complaint form and pick the licence type.
channels.note: Colorado's mental health practice act sets a filing deadline, but the Division's own pages did not state it when this was checked. Ask the Division how long you have before assuming you are out of time.

channels.name: Colorado Behavioral Health Administration
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses behavioral health entities in Colorado and takes complaints about the services they provide.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed behavioral health provider or program.
channels.how: Submit a complaint through the BHA's complaint page, or email the complaints address.

channels.name: Colorado Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide report line for child abuse and neglect. It routes the report to the county department that investigates.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Colorado program.
channels.how: Call. It is answered at any hour, every day.

channels.name: Office of Colorado's Child Protection Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office that investigates complaints about the child protection system, including how an agency handled a case, and publishes investigative reports setting out what it found. It has looked at residential child care facilities directly.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It examines how the system responded rather than licensing or prosecuting a program itself.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person who reported something to a Colorado agency and got nowhere, or who believes the response itself caused harm.
channels.how: Use the office's own complaint form.

channels.name: Disability Justice (Colorado's Protection and Advocacy agency)
channels.what_it_can_do: Colorado's federally mandated P&A, with authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Colorado program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.
channels.note: Formerly Disability Law Colorado; it now operates as Disability Justice.

civil: Colorado has no civil SOL for CSA claims against all defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for felony sex offenses against children. The SOL is 5 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for felony sex trafficking of a minor.
CSAM: There is no SOL for felony CSAM offenses.

states.note: Connecticut puts a clock on reporting: an oral report to the DCF Careline within 12 hours of the suspected abuse, followed by the written DCF-136 form within 48 hours of that. Anyone reporting in good faith is immune from civil or criminal liability. The Department of Public Health is equally clear about its own limits - it can only act against a licence, and nothing it does will get a consumer compensated.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Intentional harm such as assault, battery or false imprisonment: three years from the date of the act (not the date you discovered it). Negligence or reckless conduct: two years from when the injury was sustained or discovered, but never more than three years after the act.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Connecticut does NOT pause the civil deadline for most injuries while the victim is a child. The three-year and two-year periods run from the abuse even if the victim was a minor. Only sexual-abuse claims get special extended time.
items.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 52-577, 52-584 (no general tolling provision in chapter 926)

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Claims against the State go to the Office of the Claims Commissioner within one year of when the injury was sustained or discovered, and never more than three years after the act. Suits against a town and its employee jointly need written notice to the town clerk within six months and a lawsuit within two years.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Physical child abuse (for example, risk of injury to a child, or assault) must be charged within five years of the offense if it can carry more than a year in prison. There is no rule pausing it until the victim turns 18 for non-sexual abuse.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault: five years from the offense (no limit if it is a class A felony). Misdemeanor assault: one year.

channels.name: Connecticut Department of Public Health, Practitioner Investigations Unit
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints against the health care practitioners the Department regulates, including licensed professional counselors, clinical social workers, psychologists and marital and family therapists, and the boards act against the licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: Its jurisdiction is limited by law to action against the licence. The Department says plainly that nothing it or a board does will result in any compensation, monetary or otherwise, to the person who complained.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor, clinical social worker, psychologist or marital and family therapist in Connecticut.
channels.how: Read the Department's complaint page and its practitioner complaints FAQ first, then file. You can call to have a complaint form posted to you.
channels.phone_note: To request a complaint form by post.
channels.mail: Department of Public Health, Practitioner Investigations Unit, P.O. Box 340308, Hartford, CT 06134-0308

channels.name: Connecticut DCF Careline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect, open around the clock, and the route into a Department of Children and Families investigation.
channels.who_to_report: A child under 18 at a Connecticut program. Anyone with reasonable cause to suspect abuse may report.
channels.how: Make the oral report within 12 hours of the suspected abuse, then send the written DCF-136 form within 48 hours of that. A report can also go to a law enforcement agency.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
channels.deadline: Not a deadline on the abuse, but on the report: oral within 12 hours, written DCF-136 within 48 hours of the oral report.
channels.note: Anyone who makes a report in good faith is immune from civil and criminal liability for it.

channels.name: Connecticut Office of Early Childhood, Licensing Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child care programs and camps in Connecticut and investigates complaints against them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed child care program or camp. Where abuse or neglect is happening at one, Connecticut tells you to call the Careline as well as this division.
channels.how: Use the Office's complaint page, or call the Licensing Division.

channels.name: Disability Rights Connecticut
channels.what_it_can_do: Connecticut's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Connecticut program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims is age 51, with revival up to age 48. A narrow exception eliminates the SOL for claims against any defendant, either individual perpetrator or other, if the perpetrator of the abuse has been criminally convicted of first-degree sexual assault.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for any felony or misdemeanor CSA offense, including sexual abuse and exploitation.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking offenses.
CSAM: The SOL for child pornography violations is 5 years from the offense.

states.note: Delaware has an Institutional Abuse Unit inside the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families that investigates abuse or neglect of a child while at a facility or program, so an institutional report does not get handled as an ordinary family case. Delaware also places a duty on every licensed practitioner to report another practitioner they reasonably believe is doing something that would be grounds for discipline - useful if you are a clinician who has seen something and is wondering whether you may say so.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the date the injury happened, for any personal-injury claim, including assault, battery and negligence.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Delaware's childhood tolling rule (three years after the disability ends) only covers the claims listed in sections 8101-8115, and the two-year personal-injury deadline is section 8119, outside that range. So for physical-injury claims the clock likely runs from the injury even if the victim was a child. Only sexual-abuse claims get special treatment.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: The State and its employees are immune for good-faith discretionary acts done without gross or wanton negligence. Counties, towns and other local bodies are immune from tort suits except narrow negligence exceptions (vehicles, public buildings, pollution); a local ordinance may require notice but cannot bar a suit if notice is given within one year.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Child abuse causing permanent injury (first degree) is a class A felony and can be charged at any time. Other felony child abuse (second and third degree, child torture, felony endangering) must be charged within five years; misdemeanor child abuse within three years. The clock is not paused until the victim turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault (first or second degree) must be charged within five years; no limit if it is a class A felony. Misdemeanor assault (class A misdemeanor): three years; lesser misdemeanors: two years.

channels.name: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation
channels.what_it_can_do: Houses the Board of Mental Health and Chemical Dependency Professionals, the Board of Professional Counselors and the psychology board. The boards monitor complaints against their licensees, hold formal hearings and impose sanctions.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed mental health or chemical dependency professional in Delaware.
channels.how: Submit the complaint in writing to the Director of the Division of Professional Regulation. At the Board's next scheduled meeting a contact person is appointed and given a copy of it.
channels.note: Under Title 24 Chapter 30, every licensee has a duty to report in writing where they reasonably believe another practitioner or health care provider has engaged in conduct that would be grounds for discipline.

channels.name: Delaware Child Abuse Report Line (Institutional Abuse Unit)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory 24-hour report line. Where the complaint concerns abuse or neglect of a child while at a facility or program, the Department's Institutional Abuse Unit or law enforcement investigates it.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Delaware program.
channels.how: Call the report line at any hour.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Delaware Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL)
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints that a licensed facility has broken the licensing rules, including the regulations governing residential child care facilities.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It has no authority over financial matters and does not investigate personal disputes. Abuse and neglect go to the Child Abuse Report Line instead.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Delaware residential child care facility, where the issue is a licensing breach.
channels.how: File a confidential complaint online, or call the office for the county the facility is in.
channels.phone_note: Kent and Sussex counties; also 302-739-5487. New Castle County 302-892-5800.

channels.name: Disability Rights Delaware (Community Legal Aid Society)
channels.what_it_can_do: Delaware's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Delaware program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.
channels.note: Operates as part of the Community Legal Aid Society; its site is declasi.org.

civil: CSA: There is no SOL for civil CSA claims against any defendants.
Trafficking: The SOL is age 23 for trafficking claims.
CSAM: There is no SOL for civil CSAM claims against any defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for all felony and misdemeanor CSA crimes.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for felony trafficking violations.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM violations.

states.note: The District runs every complaint about a health professional through one investigating body, the Health Regulation and Licensing Administration, which works on behalf of all the occupation boards. It will not accept an anonymous complaint. Its boards can reprimand, impose probation, fine, suspend or revoke a licence under the Health Occupations Revision Act.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Assault, battery, false arrest and false imprisonment: one year. Negligence and other claims with no specific deadline (for example, negligent supervision by a program): three years.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18. After turning 18 they get the full normal period: one year for assault or battery (until 19), three years for negligence (until 21).

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: To sue the District of Columbia for injuries, written notice must reach the Mayor within six months of the injury (a police report made in the regular course of duty also counts). The lawsuit itself follows the normal deadlines.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Cruelty to children (first or second degree) is a felony and must be charged within six years of the offense. The clock is not paused until the victim grows up for this non-sexual crime.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault (such as aggravated assault) must be charged within six years. Misdemeanor simple assault: three years.

channels.name: DC Health Regulation and Licensing Administration (HRLA)
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints on behalf of the District's health occupation boards, including the Board of Professional Counseling, the Board of Psychology and the Board of Social Work. Disciplinary action runs from a reprimand through probation, a fine and suspension to revoking the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor, psychologist or social worker in the District.
channels.how: Complete the complaint form and send it to the board that regulates that profession.
channels.phone_note: HRLA; also 202-724-8800. Board of Professional Counseling 202-442-5955.
channels.mail: Board of Professional Counseling, 2201 Shannon Place SE, Washington, DC 20020
channels.note: The Board will not accept an anonymous complaint.

channels.name: DC Child and Family Services Agency hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The District's statutory report line, taken by CFSA's Office of Hotline and Investigations around the clock for children up to 18.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a District program.
channels.how: Call at any hour.
channels.phone_note: 202-671-SAFE. 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: DC Child and Family Services Agency, facility oversight
channels.what_it_can_do: The District's public child welfare agency, responsible for protecting children at risk of abuse and neglect and for the programs placed children are in.
channels.who_to_report: A District facility or program caring for children.
channels.how: Contact CFSA. Abuse or neglect goes to the hotline.
channels.mail: Child and Family Services Agency, 200 I Street SE, Washington, DC 20003

channels.name: University Legal Services (the District's Protection and Advocacy agency)
channels.what_it_can_do: The District's federally mandated P&A, with authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A District program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against all defendants is age 40, with a 5-year discovery rule.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for many CSA and incest offenses. The SOL is age 27 for other felonies and 3 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: The SOL is age 31 for trafficking-related felonies.
CSAM: The SOL is age 31 for CSAM offenses.

states.note: Florida runs every complaint about a licensed clinician through one portal at the Department of Health, whatever the profession, and it has a hard six-year deadline running from the last date of treatment. The facility is regulated separately by the Agency for Health Care Administration, which licenses residential treatment centers for children and adolescents, including therapeutic group homes.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Four years from the injury for assault, battery, false imprisonment or any other intentional tort. Two years from the injury for a claim based on negligence (for example, a program's careless supervision).

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Florida does not generally pause the clock for being a minor: it is paused only while the child has no parent or guardian, or the parent's interest is adverse, and never beyond 7 years from the act. But a lawsuit based on abuse (physical, mental or sexual, as defined in Florida's child-welfare law) can be filed up to 7 years after turning 18, within 4 years of leaving the abuser's dependency, or within 4 years of discovering the injury and its link to the abuse, whichever is latest.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Against the state, a county or another public agency, you must present a written claim to the agency (and, for state agencies, to the Department of Financial Services) within 3 years, and file the lawsuit within 4 years of the injury.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Aggravated child abuse (a first-degree felony) must be charged within 4 years. Child abuse without great bodily harm, and neglect, are third-degree felonies with 3 years. The clock is NOT paused until the child turns 18 for physical abuse; that rule covers only sex offenses. If the child died, there is no limit.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Aggravated assault (third-degree felony) and aggravated battery (second-degree felony) must be charged within 3 years. Simple assault must be charged within 1 year and simple battery within 2 years.

channels.name: Florida Department of Health, Medical Quality Assurance
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints against every health care practitioner the Department licenses - psychologists, clinical social workers, marriage and family therapists, mental health counselors and physicians - and can reprimand, fine, restrict practice, impose probation, suspend or revoke a licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: Everything it can do is administrative. It cannot award you damages, and it may require you to pay for copies of medical records it needs.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed clinician who treated you or your child in Florida. Verify the licence first through the Department's lookup, which also shows any disciplinary history.
channels.how: File through the Florida Health Care Complaint Portal. It cannot be done over the phone, and Florida law requires the complaint to be signed. Unlicensed practice is the exception and can be reported by phone.
channels.phone_note: 877-HALT-ULA, for unlicensed activity only. A complaint against a licensee has to be in writing.
channels.deadline: Six years from the last date of treatment, and the whole investigation and probable cause finding has to be finished inside it, so filing late in the window may leave too little time.
channels.note: Complaints stay confidential until ten days after probable cause is found, and permanently if it is not. Patient identity and records stay confidential either way. If the case is opened, the practitioner gets a copy of the complaint.

channels.name: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration, Complaint Administration Unit
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates Residential Treatment Centers for Children and Adolescents - 24-hour residential programs including therapeutic group homes - and investigates complaints about the care they give.
channels.who_to_report: The facility. Check first on FloridaHealthFinder.gov whether AHCA regulates it; if it is not AHCA-licensed it may be licensed by the Department of Children and Families instead, or by nobody.
channels.how: Use the online Health Care Facility Complaint Form, or call the complaint line. There is a separate form for reporting a facility operating without a licence.
channels.phone_note: Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm Eastern. Florida Relay TDD 1-800-955-8771.

channels.name: Florida Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse, neglect and abandonment in Florida. Where the person accused is a caregiver, the Department of Children and Families investigates; where they are not, the report is transferred electronically to the local law enforcement agency where the child lives.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Florida program. Florida law requires anyone who suspects a child has been abused by any person to report it here.
channels.how: Call, report online, or fax. Florida Relay 711 and TTY 1-800-453-5145.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, every day. Fax 1-800-914-0004.

channels.name: Disability Rights Florida
channels.what_it_can_do: Florida's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities and a right of access to them. Free legal advocacy for eligible clients.
channels.who_to_report: A Florida program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no SOL against any defendants for civil CSA claims involving sexual battery of children under age 16. The SOL is age 25, plus a 4-year discovery rule, for sexual battery claims involving 16- and 17-year-olds and any other CSA claims.
Trafficking: The general SOL for trafficking claims is age 25. Except that there is no SOL for claims against an adult theater for trafficking children under age 16.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM claims is age 25.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for some felony CSA offenses. The SOL for any remaining CSA felonies is age 21, and the SOL for misdemeanors is 2 years from the offense.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for sex trafficking offenses.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM felonies is age 21, while the SOL for CSAM misdemeanors is 2 years from the offense.

states.note: Two things to know about Georgia before you file. The licensing boards will not accept a complaint without the licensee's name and licence number, so look them up first. And several of the outcomes a board can reach - a letter of concern, a private consent order - are confidential and will never be published, so a program's clean public record does not prove nothing was found.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for any personal injury claim, whether it is assault, battery, false imprisonment or negligence. If the injury came from a crime, the clock is paused while the criminal case is pending, for up to 6 years.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. If you were under 18 when you were hurt, the two years do not start until your 18th birthday, so the deadline is your 20th birthday. There is no cap in the statute.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Against the state, written notice must be sent within 12 months of discovering the loss and the lawsuit filed within 2 years; against a county the claim must be presented within 12 months, and against a city within 6 months. The state cannot be sued at all for assault, battery or false imprisonment by its employees, only for negligence.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felonies against a child under 18, including second-degree cruelty to children, must be charged within 7 years. First-degree cruelty to children (maliciously causing a child cruel or excessive physical or mental pain) can be charged at any time if the child was under 16 and the crime happened on or after July 1, 2012.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Aggravated assault, like most felonies, must be charged within 4 years (7 years if the victim was under 18). Misdemeanor simple assault or battery must be charged within 2 years.

channels.name: Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers and Marriage and Family Therapists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors, social workers and marriage and family therapists. Where a complaint substantiates unlicensed practice, or somebody aiding unlicensed practice, the board can move to a cease and desist order or refer it for criminal prosecution.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It has no power over an unlicensed individual or facility unless they apply for a licence. Investigations are confidential by law, and the board will not tell you over the phone whether it even received your complaint.
channels.who_to_report: A counselor, social worker or marriage and family therapist licensed in Georgia. Psychologists have their own board under the same Secretary of State division and the same process.
channels.how: Use the Secretary of State's licensing complaint route. You must give the licensee's name and licence number - find them in the licensee search - and attach any supporting documents.
channels.note: Complaints and everything about them are exempt from open records and strictly confidential. Of the ways a case can close, only a public consent order and an order for monies received become public; a letter of concern and a private consent order do not.

channels.name: Georgia DHS, Office of Inspector General, Residential Child Care Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Monitors, inspects and licenses residential child care facilities, programs and services, including Child Caring Institutions - the group homes and institutions providing full-time care for six or more children away from their own homes. It investigates complaints against them.
channels.who_to_report: The facility. If you know its name or address you can go straight into the public complaint portal.
channels.how: Use the public complaint portal, or email the full details to the reports address. Give your contact information if you want to be told what the investigation found; it is kept confidential.
channels.note: You can complain anonymously, but the unit says it needs your contact details to come back to you with the result.

channels.name: Georgia Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting (DFCS)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect in Georgia, staffed seven days a week. A report starts a Division of Family and Children Services response.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Georgia program right now.
channels.how: Call the hotline. Mandated reporters can also submit a referral through the online child protective services portal.

channels.name: Georgia Office of the Child Advocate
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent state office that reviews how the child protection system handles cases and takes complaints about it. The route when a report has already gone in and nothing has moved.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the state's handling rather than licensing or prosecuting the program itself.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person who has already reported and got nowhere.

channels.name: Georgia Advocacy Office
channels.what_it_can_do: Georgia's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Georgia program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM offenses against all defendants is age 23 with a 2-year discovery rule.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL in Georgia for many felony CSA crimes against children under age sixteen, including rape. The SOL is age 31 for forcible rape of a sixteen-year-old and age 32 for forcible rape of a seventeen-year-old. The SOL is 7 years from the offense for remaining felonies and 2 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: The SOL for felony CSAM violation is 7 years from the offense. The SOL for misdemeanor CSAM violations is 2 years from the offense.

states.note: Hawaii has a name for what happens in these places: Institutional Harm, meaning abuse or neglect in any substitute care arrangement the Department licenses - foster, group or child care. Its Child Welfare Intake Unit takes Institutional Harm reports around the clock alongside ordinary abuse reports, which means you do not have to argue about which category your call belongs in.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years for any personal injury, whether it was assault, battery, false imprisonment or negligence. Hawaii courts start the two years when the person knew, or should have known, of the injury and who caused it.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. If you were under 18 when you were hurt, the two years start on your 18th birthday, so the deadline is your 20th birthday. The statute has no cap.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: A lawsuit against the State must be filed within two years of the injury, and the State cannot be sued under its tort claims law for assault, battery or false imprisonment by its employees. For a county, written notice is required within two years.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Hawaii has no separate felony crime of physical child abuse; it is charged as assault or as endangering the welfare of a minor. Those felonies must be charged within 3 years (6 years for a class A felony). The clock is not paused until the child turns 18 for physical abuse.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Assault in the first degree (class B felony) and second degree (class C felony) must be charged within 3 years. Misdemeanor assault must be charged within 2 years (1 year for a petty misdemeanor).

channels.name: Hawaii Regulated Industries Complaints Office (RICO)
channels.what_it_can_do: The licence-enforcement arm of the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs. It reviews complaints against licensees of the professional boards - psychologists, marriage and family therapists, clinical social workers, physicians and psychiatrists among them - files administrative actions against them, and sues people providing those services with no board licence at all.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed mental health professional in Hawaii, or somebody practising without a licence.
channels.how: Use the Health Care Provider Complaint Form from the Professional and Vocational Licensing pages.
channels.note: The Resource Center will tell you a licensee's current status and whether they have a prior complaint history, which is worth asking before you file.

channels.name: Hawaii Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line. The Child Welfare Intake Unit takes reports around the clock, including Institutional Harm reports - abuse or neglect in any substitute care arrangement the Department licenses.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Hawaii program.
channels.how: Call. From the neighbour islands there is a toll-free number.
channels.phone_note: Oahu. Toll free from the neighbour islands, 1-888-380-3088. 24 hours a day.

channels.name: Hawaii DHS child care and residential licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses Hawaii's substitute care arrangements and decides whether a complaint discloses a breach of the child care law or licensing rules that needs investigating.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Hawaii facility, where the issue is a licensing breach. Abuse or neglect goes to the hotline instead, and the Department says so directly.
channels.how: Report to the licensing unit for the facility.

channels.name: Hawaii Disability Rights Center
channels.what_it_can_do: Hawaii's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Hawaii program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: The civil CSA SOL is age 26 or 3 years from discovery as against perpetrators. The SOL is age 20 or 2 years from discovery as against other defendants.
Trafficking: The SOL is age 24 for sex trafficking claims.
CSAM: The SOL is age 26 for CSAM claims.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for some sexual assault felonies, and an SOL of ages 21 and 24 for other felonies. The SOL for misdemeanors is two years from the offense.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for sex trafficking felonies.
CSAM: The SOL for first-degree felony CSAM offenses is age 24, while the SOL for second- and third-degree felony CSAM offenses is age 21.

states.note: Idaho has a trap worth knowing before you pick up the phone. The child protection division's role is limited to what happens in a family home: where the person who harmed a child does not live with them, as in any residential program, the report is forwarded to law enforcement instead of being investigated by child protection. So for abuse inside a program, the police and the licensing division are the substantive channels, and the hotline is the way in rather than the destination.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years for a personal injury claim, including negligence, and two years for assault, battery or false imprisonment. The clock starts when the harm happens, not when it is discovered. A child physically injured under Idaho's injury-to-a-child law has a longer, separate deadline (see the minors section).

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For a child hurt by physical abuse that counts as the crime of injury to a child, the lawsuit can be filed up to 5 years after turning 18, or within 5 years of discovering the abuse and its link to the injury, whichever is later. That claim can also be brought against the abuser's employer. For other injuries, being a minor pauses the two-year clock, but for no more than 6 years.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: A written claim must be filed within 180 days (with the Secretary of State for the state, or the clerk for a county or city), and the lawsuit within 2 years. Minors get until 180 days after turning 18 (or 6 years, whichever is earlier), and child-abuse claims follow the 5-years-after-18 rule. Governments cannot be sued for assault, battery or false imprisonment by employees acting without malice or criminal intent.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony injury to a child (causing or permitting a child to suffer physical pain or injury in conditions likely to cause great bodily harm or death) must be charged within 5 years. Misdemeanor injury to a child must be charged within 1 year. The clock is not paused until the child turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault or battery (for example aggravated assault or aggravated battery) must be charged within 5 years. Misdemeanor assault or battery must be charged within 1 year.

channels.name: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses (DOPL)
channels.what_it_can_do: Houses the boards for professional counselors and marriage and family therapists, psychologist examiners, and social work examiners, and runs a single complaint and investigation process for all of them. Where a formal administrative complaint is filed, an independent administrative law judge holds an evidentiary hearing.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: If there is no jurisdiction, or no possible breach of that board's own laws and rules, no case is opened at all.
channels.who_to_report: A counselor, marriage and family therapist, psychologist or social worker licensed in Idaho.
channels.how: File through the Division's complaint page. It decides first whether there is jurisdiction, then whether to assign an investigator.

channels.name: Idaho DHW, Children's Residential Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses children's residential care facilities, children's agencies and children's therapeutic outdoor programs under IDAPA 16.04.18, and investigates complaints against them. Its representatives must be given access to the program, its grounds and its records to investigate a complaint - a real power in an industry that relies on keeping people out.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: Idaho exempts a good deal from licensing, including facilities operating as private or religious schools. An exempt program is outside this channel, which is exactly the gap several Idaho programs have operated in.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed children's residential care facility or therapeutic outdoor program. If the program claims to be a private or religious school, check whether anybody licenses it at all.
channels.how: Call the complaint line or email.

channels.name: Idaho Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes reports of child abuse, neglect and abandonment around the clock. Where the person who harmed the child does not live in their home, the report is forwarded to law enforcement - which is the usual position for abuse inside a program.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Idaho program. Idaho Code 16-1605 requires everyone in Idaho to report suspected abuse, neglect or abandonment, with a narrow exception for clergy.
channels.how: Call. You do not have to be sure, and you do not have to prove anything first; the Department says to let it or law enforcement decide. Report within 24 hours of becoming aware if you can.
channels.phone_note: 855-552-KIDS. In the Treasure Valley, 208-334-5437. 24 hours a day.
channels.note: Callers may stay anonymous, and the Department says it does not disclose caller information to the family. Reporting in good faith carries immunity from civil liability.

channels.name: DisAbility Rights Idaho
channels.what_it_can_do: Idaho's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy. In a state where much of the industry sits outside licensing, a P&A investigation may be the only outside look a program ever gets.
channels.who_to_report: An Idaho program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims is age 23 with a 5-year discovery rule against all defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for rape, sexual abuse, or lewd conduct. For other felonies, the SOL expires 5 years from the offense. For misdemeanors, the SOL is 1 year after the offense.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking is 5 years from the offense for felonies and 1 year from the offense for misdemeanors.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM is 5 years from the offense for felonies and 1 year from the offense for misdemeanors.

states.note: Illinois has a practical shortcut worth knowing: if a facility has broken state licensing standards, you can call the child abuse hotline and say you want to make a licensing complaint. That is the state's own advice, and it saves working out which of the licensing offices covers a program. Every complaint about a licensed clinician, whatever the profession, goes to one intake unit at IDFPR.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for personal injury claims, including assault, battery, negligence and false imprisonment. If the person who hurt you was convicted of a Class X or Class 1 felony (or first degree murder) for it, there is no deadline to sue that person.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. If you were under 18 when you were hurt, you have 2 years after your 18th birthday (until age 20) to sue. The statute sets no cap.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Against a local government (county, city, school district) or its employees, the lawsuit must be filed within 1 year. Claims against the State of Illinois go to the Court of Claims: file within 2 years (minors have 2 years after turning 18), and file a notice with the Attorney General and the Court of Claims clerk within 1 year unless the claim itself is filed within that year.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Illinois has no special deadline for physical child abuse: felonies such as aggravated battery of a child or felony child endangerment must be charged within 3 years. The clock is not paused until the child turns 18 for physical abuse.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony aggravated battery or aggravated assault must be charged within 3 years. Misdemeanor assault or battery must be charged within 1 year and 6 months.

channels.name: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation, Division of Professional Regulation
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors, clinical social workers, psychologists and marriage and family therapists among more than a hundred professions, and investigates complaints against any of them through one Complaint Intake Unit.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed mental health professional in Illinois. Complaints are accepted from clients, families, colleagues and anybody else.
