channels.how: File through the Division's complaint page. The licensee is notified of the allegations in writing once it is logged.

channels.name: Illinois DCFS Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child care and child welfare facilities in Illinois against state licensing standards, and investigates complaints that a facility has breached them.
channels.who_to_report: A facility you believe has broken licensing standards - staffing, supervision, conditions, how children are treated.
channels.how: Complain to the local DCFS Licensing Office, or call the Child Abuse Hotline and say you want to make a licensing complaint. Complaints can be made by post, email, fax or in person.
channels.phone_note: The Child Abuse Hotline also takes licensing complaints - say that is what you are calling about.

channels.name: Illinois DCFS Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour line for reporting a child harmed or at risk of harm through abuse or neglect, and the route into a DCFS investigation.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Illinois program.
channels.how: Call, at any hour.

channels.name: Equip for Equality
channels.what_it_can_do: Illinois's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Illinois program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: There is no civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, or CSAM claims against any defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for felony and misdemeanor sex offenses committed against children.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking is age 43.
CSAM: There is no SOL for creating child pornography. Lesser CSAM offenses have an SOL of age 19 or 3 years from the offense, whichever is later.

states.note: Indiana is the state where a complaint about a therapist does not start at the licensing board at all. It goes to the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division, which reviews it and only then takes it to the relevant board asking for action against the licence. Indiana also protects reporters unusually firmly: state law requires the Department of Child Services to keep the identity of anyone reporting abuse confidential.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for any personal injury claim, including assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. A person who was under 18 when hurt has 2 years after turning 18 (until age 20) to sue. The statute sets no cap.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Before suing, written notice is required: within 270 days of the injury for the State (to the Attorney General or the agency), or within 180 days for a county, city, school or other local body. The lawsuit itself follows the normal two-year deadline.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Most felony child abuse (battery on a child, or neglect of a dependent, which includes cruel confinement or restraining a child with handcuffs, rope or tape) must be charged within 5 years. The most serious grades (Level 1 or 2 felonies, such as neglect causing death or catastrophic injury to a child under 14, or battery causing death of a child under 14) can be charged at any time. The clock is not paused until the child turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony battery (Level 3 to 6) must be charged within 5 years; Level 1 and 2 felonies have no limit. Misdemeanor battery must be charged within 2 years.

channels.name: Indiana Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division (licensing complaints)
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints from the public against licensed professionals, reviews them first, and where it finds merit brings the case to the relevant board - the Behavioral Health and Human Services Licensing Board, or the Psychology Board - seeking action against the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed social worker, marriage and family therapist, mental health counselor, clinical addiction counselor or psychologist in Indiana.
channels.how: Obtain the complaint form from the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division and file it there, not with the licensing agency.

channels.name: Indiana Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour report line run by the Department of Child Services. It also connects families with no open case to free home-based services.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Indiana program.
channels.how: Call, at any hour including weekends and holidays. If every line is busy, there is a second number. Press option 2 instead if you want a referral to local support rather than to make a report.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day. If the lines are down, 1-833-800-5556.
channels.note: You can report anonymously, and even if you give your name, Indiana law requires the Department to keep the identity and contact details of every report source confidential.

channels.name: Indiana DCS Ombudsman Bureau
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints about the Department of Child Services itself - how it handled a case, or failed to.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the agency, not the program.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person whose report to DCS went nowhere.

channels.name: Indiana Disability Rights
channels.what_it_can_do: Indiana's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Indiana program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

channels.name: Indiana DCS Residential Licensing Unit
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child caring institutions, private secure facilities, group homes and emergency shelters in Indiana. Its Residential Licensing Unit reviews every institutional report of alleged child abuse or neglect connected to a licensed facility - including reports that were screened out - to decide whether the facility broke its licence or its contract.
channels.who_to_report: A DCS-licensed residential facility. The Indiana Department of Health separately runs at least annual unannounced health, food and sanitation surveys of these same facilities.
channels.how: An institutional report goes in through the child abuse hotline; the Residential Licensing Unit picks it up from there.
channels.phone_note: The child abuse hotline is the intake route for institutional reports.
channels.note: That the Unit reviews even screened-out reports matters: a report that child protection declines to investigate can still count against the facility's licence.

civil: The SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM civil claims is age 20 against all defendants, or a period of time from discovery, elimination of dependency status, or criminal conviction.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for Class A felony rape. The SOL for other offenses varies from age 31, to 10 years after the offense, or 4 years after the victim ceases to be a dependent of the perpetrator.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for felony child sex trafficking.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is 10 years from the offense or 4 years after the victim ceases to be a dependent of the perpetrator, whichever is later.

states.note: Iowa runs a separate number for abuse suspected inside a licensed facility or program, distinct from the general child abuse hotline - use it if what happened was inside a program. Iowa also folded its Board of Psychology into the Board of Behavioral Health Professionals in 2024, so one board now covers psychologists along with counselors and social workers. And the Iowa Office of Ombudsman covers both the licensing boards and Health and Human Services, which makes it the escalation route when either one stalls.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for any personal injury claim, including assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. As of July 1, 2026, someone injured as a child has until five years after turning 18 (age 23) to sue. Before that change the extension was only one year after turning 18. It also applies to claims against the state and local governments.
items.citation: Iowa Code § 614.8(2), as amended by 2026 Iowa Acts, HF 1036, § 5 (effective July 1, 2026)

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Against the State of Iowa, a written claim must be filed with the Department of Management within two years; the State cannot be sued for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Against a city, county or school district, the lawsuit must be filed within two years of the injury. Minors get the extension described above in both cases.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony child endangerment against a child under 18 (causing bodily injury, serious injury or death) can be charged at any time; there is no deadline. Misdemeanor child endangerment must be charged within 3 years.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Felony assault (for example, assault causing serious injury) must be charged within 3 years. Iowa uses the same 3 years for aggravated and serious misdemeanor assault; simple misdemeanor assault must be charged within 1 year.

channels.name: Iowa Board of Behavioral Health Professionals
channels.what_it_can_do: Receives and investigates complaints against mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, social workers, behavior analysts and - since the boards merged under 2024 Iowa Acts SF 2385 - psychologists, and disciplines their licences. Iowa publishes its discipline documents.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed behavioral health professional in Iowa. Anyone may file: a patient, a family member, anyone else.
channels.how: File through the Department of Inspections, Appeals and Licensing complaints page, which routes it to the right board.
channels.note: Iowa law keeps the complainant's information confidential.

channels.name: Iowa reporting of abuse in a licensed facility
channels.what_it_can_do: The route Iowa gives for abuse suspected inside a licensed facility or program, separate from the general child abuse hotline.
channels.who_to_report: A young person abused inside an Iowa licensed facility or program.
channels.how: Call the facility line rather than the general hotline.
channels.phone_note: For abuse suspected in a licensed facility or program.

channels.name: Iowa Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide confidential 24-hour line taking reports of suspected abuse of children and dependent adults. The Child Protective Services intake unit screens them.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Iowa program.
channels.how: Call. Have identifying details and the child's whereabouts ready.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
channels.note: You may stay anonymous unless you are reporting as a mandatory reporter, in which case you have to leave your name and contact details.

channels.name: Iowa Office of Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office that reviews complaints about state agencies, and it names both the professional licensing boards and the Department of Health and Human Services among the bodies it covers. The route when a licensing complaint or an abuse report has gone nowhere.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It examines how an agency handled something rather than disciplining a clinician or a program itself.
channels.who_to_report: Somebody who has already complained to an Iowa board or to HHS and got no response they can make sense of.

channels.name: Disability Rights Iowa
channels.what_it_can_do: Iowa's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Iowa program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

channels.name: Iowa HHS facility licensing and certification
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and certifies Iowa's residential facilities and programs for children, and takes the complaints about abuse inside them through its dedicated facility reporting line.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Iowa facility or program.
channels.how: Use the facility abuse line for abuse inside a licensed program, and the Department's contacts page for anything else.
channels.phone_note: For abuse suspected in a licensed facility or program.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims is age 19 against all defendants, with some limited rules for abuse by a counselor, instructor, or school employee, and a discovery rule of 2 to 4 years.
criminal: There is no SOL for all CSA, trafficking, and CSAM felonies and misdemeanors.

states.note: Kansas splits the work usefully: the Department for Children and Families investigates abuse or neglect alleged to have happened in a childcare or residential care facility, and it is required to pass any investigation involving a licensed facility straight to the Department of Health and Environment, which holds the licence. So one call to the Protection Report Center reaches both the investigation and the licensor.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Only one year for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Two years for negligence and other injury claims, starting when the injury is substantial or reasonably discoverable, but never more than 10 years after the act.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes, but briefly. Someone injured as a child gets one year after turning 18 to sue, and in no case more than 8 years after the act that caused the injury.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Before suing a Kansas city, county, school district or other municipality, a written notice of claim must be filed with its clerk or governing body; you then wait for denial or 120 days. The lawsuit must still be filed within the normal deadline (1 or 2 years), with at least 90 days after denial.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Abuse of a child (torturing, cruelly beating, cruel corporal punishment, or cruel physical restraint such as caging or binding a child under 18) must be charged within 5 years. The clock does not run while the crime is concealed, and in some child cases it can be extended until the victim turns 28.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Aggravated assault and aggravated battery must be charged within 5 years. Kansas uses the same 5 years for misdemeanor assault and battery.

channels.name: Kansas Behavioral Sciences Regulatory Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Regulates psychologists, social workers, professional counselors, marriage and family therapists, addiction counselors and behavior analysts, and disciplines their licences. Every complaint gets a case number, and once the Board decides to investigate, the licensee is told what is alleged.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says plainly that it does not represent individuals and does not obtain compensation on anyone's behalf.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed behavioral health professional in Kansas - one board covers all of them.
channels.how: Complete the Board's Report of Alleged Violation. All complaints must be in writing.
channels.mail: Kansas Behavioral Sciences Regulatory Board, Eisenhower State Office Building, 700 SW Harrison St, Ste 420, Topeka, KS 66603-3817

channels.name: Kansas Department of Health and Environment, child care licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Administers the Kansas child care licensing law and issues the licences. Where there is a regulatory concern it is required to carry out an on-site complaint survey to check whether the facility complies.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Kansas facility, where the problem is a regulatory breach.
channels.how: File through the Department's complaint page, or call its complaint hotline.
channels.note: A regulatory complaint forces an on-site survey; that is the practical value of using this channel alongside the abuse report.

channels.name: Kansas Protection Report Center
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation of children and adults. The Department for Children and Families receives, investigates and assesses allegations of abuse or neglect said to have happened in a childcare or residential care facility, and must promptly report any investigation involving a licensed facility to the Department of Health and Environment.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Kansas program.
channels.how: Call, or report online. Lines are staffed around the clock.
channels.note: Kansas says every call is taken seriously and every effort is made to protect the caller's identity.

channels.name: Disability Rights Center of Kansas
channels.what_it_can_do: Kansas's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Kansas program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM civil claims against all defendants is the later of age 31 or 3 years from criminal conviction, with revival up to these age and conviction time limits.
criminal: CSA: There is no criminal SOL for most CSA felonies, an SOL of age 28 for other sexually violent felonies, and an SOL of 5 years from the offense for any remaining felonies and misdemeanors, with a limited DNA rule.
Trafficking: There is no criminal SOL for most Trafficking felonies, including aggravated human trafficking.
CSAM: There is no criminal SOL for most CSAM felonies, including internet trading in child pornography.

states.note: Kentucky's hotline is answered by people around the clock, but its online reporting form is only monitored on weekdays between 8am and 4:30pm Eastern - so an urgent report at a weekend has to be a phone call, not a form. Its counseling board is unusually clear about what happens next: it acknowledges a written complaint within two business days, sends a copy to the counselor for a response, and puts both in front of the board at its next meeting.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: One year from the injury for a personal injury claim, whether it is assault, battery or negligence. This is one of the shortest deadlines in the country.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. For someone injured as a child, the one year starts on the 18th birthday, so the deadline is the 19th birthday. There is no cap. This does NOT apply to claims against the state through the Board of Claims.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Injury claims against the Commonwealth go to the Board of Claims and must be filed within one year of discovering the injury, and never more than two years after the act. Being a minor does NOT extend this: a parent or guardian must file within the same deadline.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Kentucky has no time limit for any felony. Felony criminal abuse or neglect of a child (serious injury, torture, cruel confinement or cruel punishment) and felony assault on a child can be charged at any time. Misdemeanor abuse must be charged within 1 year.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: No time limit for felony assault (first, second or third degree). Misdemeanor assault (fourth degree) must be charged within 1 year.

channels.name: Kentucky Board of Licensed Professional Counselors
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints that a counselor has breached Kentucky's statutes or regulations, and disciplines the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor in Kentucky.
channels.how: Send a written complaint to the Board. It must be in writing and signed by whoever is making it.
channels.mail: Kentucky Board of Licensed Professional Counselors, 500 Mero Street 2SC32, Frankfort, KY 40601
channels.note: The Board acknowledges a written complaint within two business days, sends the counselor a copy and asks for a response, then puts your complaint and their answer to the board at its next scheduled meeting.

channels.name: Kentucky Board of Social Work
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints that a social worker has breached Kentucky's statutes or regulations, and disciplines the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed social worker in Kentucky.
channels.how: Use the Board's online complaint form.

channels.name: Kentucky Board of Examiners of Psychology
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in Kentucky.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist.
channels.how: Contact the Board for its complaint process.

channels.name: Kentucky child abuse and neglect hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse, neglect and dependency, run by the Department for Community Based Services, which investigates through its regional offices covering all 120 counties.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Kentucky program.
channels.how: Call. Staff answer 24 hours a day including weekends and holidays. There is an online form as well, but it is only monitored 8am to 4:30pm Eastern on weekdays, so use the phone if it is urgent or out of hours.
channels.phone_note: 877-KYSAFE1. Answered 24 hours a day, every day.

channels.name: Kentucky Protection and Advocacy
channels.what_it_can_do: Kentucky's federally mandated P&A, with authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Kentucky program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

channels.name: Kentucky Division of Regulated Child Care (DRCC)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and investigates complaints against residential child caring facilities and child placing agencies in Kentucky, as well as child care centres. It also takes reports of child care operating without approval at all.
channels.who_to_report: A residential child caring facility, or a program you believe is operating unapproved.
channels.how: Call the DRCC call centre or email it.
channels.note: DRCC says its staff will not give the provider the name of whoever reported them during an investigation.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims in Kentucky is age 28 against all defendants, with 10-year discovery and criminal conviction rules.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for CSA felonies, and the SOL for misdemeanor sex offenses is age 28.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking felonies, and the SOL for misdemeanor trafficking offenses is age 28.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM felonies, and the SOL for misdemeanor CSAM offenses is age 28.

states.note: Louisiana's child protection hotline explicitly covers abuse and neglect inside licensed residential and treatment facilities, not only in family homes, so it is the right call for something that happened in a program. Its counseling board, by contrast, will not accept an anonymous complaint at all unless the documents you send with it plainly show a breach of law on their own.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the day of the injury for a delictual (tort) claim, including battery, false imprisonment and negligence, for injuries on or after July 1, 2024. Injuries before July 1, 2024 fell under the old one-year period. Injuries from a crime of violence also have two years.
items.citation: La. Civ. Code art. 3493.1; La. Civ. Code art. 3493.3

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Louisiana does not pause the clock for children in general: prescription runs against minors, so a parent or guardian must sue within the normal period. But a claim for physical abuse of a minor that caused permanent impairment, permanent physical injury or scarring never expires, and neither does a claim against someone convicted of a crime against the child.
items.citation: La. R.S. 9:2800.9(A); La. Civ. Code art. 3468

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Louisiana has no general advance notice-of-claim requirement for suits against the state or local governments; the normal two-year delictual period applies, but service on the government defendant must be requested within 90 days of filing suit or the suit can be dismissed.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Cruelty to juveniles: four years (six years if the child was eight or younger, or for second degree cruelty causing serious injury). When the victim was under 18, the clock does not start until the victim turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Four years for aggravated battery and other felonies not necessarily punished at hard labor; six years for felonies that must be punished at hard labor. Misdemeanor assault or battery: two years.

channels.name: Louisiana Licensed Professional Counselors Board of Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Receives complaints against licensed professional counselors, provisional licensed professional counselors, and licensed and provisional marriage and family therapists, and disciplines their licences through its Disciplinary Committee.
channels.who_to_report: An LPC, PLPC, LMFT or PLMFT in Louisiana.
channels.how: Use the Board's online complaint form. Include your contact details.
channels.note: Anonymous complaints are not accepted unless the documentation you provide clearly shows a violation of law by itself. The administrator first checks whether the person is within the Board's jurisdiction at all.

channels.name: Louisiana State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in Louisiana, and exists in statute to protect the public from unauthorised, unqualified and improper practice of psychology.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist in Louisiana, or somebody practising psychology without authorisation.
channels.how: Submit a complaint through the Board's portal.

channels.name: Louisiana Child Protection Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line, run by the Department of Children and Family Services, which is mandated to receive and investigate reports of child abuse and neglect - including abuse or neglect occurring in licensed DCFS or Department of Health residential and treatment facilities.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Louisiana program, including abuse, neglect, sexual abuse and juvenile sex trafficking.
channels.how: Call. It is open every hour of every day of the year, and all calls are confidential.
channels.phone_note: 855-4LA-KIDS. 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

channels.name: Disability Rights Louisiana
channels.what_it_can_do: Louisiana's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Louisiana program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

channels.name: Louisiana DCFS Licensing Section (Residential Care)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child residential facilities and child placing agencies in Louisiana and enforces the Child Care Facilities and Child Placing Agencies Licensing Act. It has revoked licences and sought injunctions against unlicensed providers.
channels.who_to_report: A child residential facility. Louisiana defines a complaint broadly: any allegation that someone is breaching the standards, or acting or failing to act in a way that harms the health, safety, rights or welfare of a child living there.
channels.how: Contact the Licensing Section. It aims to inspect every residential licensing complaint within 30 days.
channels.phone_note: Licensing staff, 8:00am to 4:30pm weekdays except legal holidays.
channels.note: Louisiana publishes a list of every currently licensed facility, so it is worth checking whether a program holds a licence at all.

civil: Louisiana has no civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, or CSAM claims against all defendants. A 3-year revival window is open until June 14, 2027 for all previously expired claims against any type of defendant.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for aggravated and forcible rape, an SOL of age 48 for other felonies, and an SOL of 2 years from the offense for certain misdemeanors, with a limited DNA rule.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking is age 48.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is age 48.

states.note: Maine runs one number for two different jobs: 1-800-452-1999 takes reports of suspected child abuse and it takes licensing concerns about a children's residential facility, because the same Office of Child and Family Services unit licenses and investigates them. Maine also has an independent Child Welfare Ombudsman, outside the department, for when the department itself is the problem.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Six years from the injury, for assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence alike.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For someone injured as a child, the six years start when they turn 18, so the deadline is normally the 24th birthday. There is no separate longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Under the Maine Tort Claims Act, written notice must be filed within 365 days, and suit within 2 years; if the claimant was a minor, suit may be brought within 2 years after turning 18.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Maine has no separate physical child abuse crime; it is charged as assault or endangering the welfare of a child. Six years for Class A, B or C crimes (such as assault on a child under 6, or aggravated assault) and three years for Class D or E crimes (such as simple assault or endangering the welfare of a child), counted from the crime, with no delay until the child turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Aggravated assault (Class A or B): six years from the crime. Simple assault (Class D): three years.

channels.name: Maine Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation
channels.what_it_can_do: Houses the Board of Counseling Professionals Licensure, the Board of Examiners of Psychologists and the State Board of Social Worker Licensure, and takes complaints against all of them through one form. Complaints, investigations and legal negotiations are handled by the Office's own investigators and attorneys.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor, psychologist or social worker in Maine.
channels.how: File through the Office's online complaint form.

channels.name: Maine OCFS, Children's Licensing and Investigation Unit
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and oversees every children's residential facility in Maine, including shelters, along with child placing agencies and child care providers, and investigates complaints against them.
channels.who_to_report: A children's residential facility - licensing violations as well as suspected abuse or neglect inside one.
channels.how: Call the same number used for child abuse reports and say it is a licensing concern about a facility.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including holidays.

channels.name: Maine OCFS Intake (child abuse and neglect)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for suspected child abuse and neglect in Maine, staffed around the clock including holidays.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Maine program.
channels.how: Call.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including holidays.

channels.name: Maine Child Welfare Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office, outside the Department of Health and Human Services, that takes complaints about how the Department is handling a child's case.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the Department's conduct rather than licensing or prosecuting a program.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person who believes the Department has mishandled a child's case, including after a report was made.
channels.how: Submit a complaint through the office's site, or call.

channels.name: Disability Rights Maine
channels.what_it_can_do: Maine's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Maine program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: There is no civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims, and all claims against all defendants are permanently revived.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for certain CSA crimes, an SOL of either 6 or 20 years from the offense for remaining felonies, and an SOL of 3 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.

CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM violations that include intentionally subjecting the victim to sexual contact. Remaining CSAM offenses have an SOL of either 3 or 6 years, depending on the seriousness of the crime.

states.note: Maryland reports abuse to the local department of social services or to local police rather than to a single statewide intake, though 1-800-91-PREVENT will take the call. It also licenses Residential Child Care programs as their own category through the Department of Human Services. One useful piece of Maryland law: since October 2016, where a local department believes a mandated reporter knowingly failed to report, it must file a complaint with that reporter's own licensing board.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Three years from the injury for battery, false imprisonment and negligence. A claim for assault alone (a threat without physical contact) has only one year.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For someone injured as a child, the clock starts at 18: three years for battery or negligence (so by the 21st birthday), and one year for assault alone. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Against the State: a written claim to the State Treasurer within 1 year of the injury, and suit within 3 years. Against a county or city: written notice within 1 year of the injury under the Local Government Tort Claims Act.
items.citation: Md. Code, State Gov't § 12-106; Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-304

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: No time limit. Child abuse by a parent, household member or anyone with care or custody of a minor is a felony in Maryland, and Maryland has no statute of limitations for felonies.
items.citation: Md. Code, Crim. Law § 3-601; Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-106(a)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: No time limit for first degree assault, a felony. Second degree assault is a misdemeanor; ordinary misdemeanors must be charged within one year, but Maryland exempts misdemeanors that can be punished with a penitentiary sentence, and whether second degree assault falls under that exemption is not settled here.
items.citation: Md. Code, Crim. Law §§ 3-202, 3-203; Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-106(a)

channels.name: Maryland Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors and therapists, including marriage and family therapists and alcohol and drug counselors. Where the Board votes to investigate, it assigns its own investigator, and a thorough investigation has to come before any charge against a licensee.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says many financial and interpersonal issues fall outside its jurisdiction because no breach of the Professional Counselors Act is involved. It cannot help you sue for money or settle a fee dispute.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor or therapist in Maryland. Psychologists and social workers have separate boards.
channels.how: File through the Board's complaint gateway. Complaints are taken from patients, family members and any other member of the public.

channels.name: Maryland Board of Examiners of Psychologists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists and registered psychology associates in Maryland.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist or registered psychology associate.
channels.how: Complete the Board's complaint form - there are separate written instructions for filling it in - and send it to the Board.

channels.name: Maryland DHS, Licensing and Monitoring (Residential Child Care)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and monitors Residential Child Care programs in Maryland as a distinct category, and takes complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed residential child care program.
channels.how: Contact the Department of Human Services.

channels.name: Maryland child abuse and neglect reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a child protective services investigation. Reports go to the local department of social services for the county the child is in, or to local law enforcement.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Maryland program.
channels.how: Call the local department of social services, or 1-800-91-PREVENT, or 911 in an emergency. Report orally straight away; a mandated reporter must also file a written report within 48 hours.

channels.name: Disability Rights Maryland
channels.what_it_can_do: Maryland's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Maryland program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: There is no SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims, and all claims against all defendants are permanently revived.
criminal: There is no criminal SOL for any felonies or misdemeanors under common law, including all CSA, trafficking, and CSAM crimes.

states.note: Massachusetts calls a child abuse report a 51A, after the section of law that creates it, and you will hear that shorthand from every agency in the state. The Department of Early Education and Care licenses the residential and congregate care programs themselves, which is not where most people would think to look, and the state also has an independent Office of the Child Advocate covering every child-serving agency.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Three years from when the claim arises, for assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence alike (all are tort actions).

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: If the injured person was a minor, the three years start when they turn 18, so the deadline is normally the 21st birthday. There is no separate longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Against a public employer, a written claim must be presented within two years (to the Attorney General for the state, or the mayor, city manager or similar official for a city or town), and suit must be filed within three years; public employers are not liable for intentional torts like assault and battery under this act.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Assault and battery on a child causing injury: six years from the crime. Wanton or reckless conduct that puts a child at substantial risk of serious bodily injury (ch. 265, § 13L) has no time limit, though a case filed more than 27 years later needs corroborating evidence.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Six years from the crime for assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, assault and battery causing serious injury, and most other assaults. Simple (misdemeanor) assault and battery: also six years.

channels.name: Massachusetts Division of Occupational Licensure, Office of Investigations
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints against licensed mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, psychiatric nurse mental health specialists, psychologists and social workers, and the boards discipline those who breach the licensing regulations.
channels.who_to_report: Any of those licence types in Massachusetts.
channels.how: File through the Commonwealth's ePLACE portal, or call or write the Office of Investigations and ask for a complaint form. File a separate complaint for each person or facility.
channels.phone_note: Board of Registration of Allied Mental Health and Human Services Professions, 9am to 5pm weekdays.
channels.note: Be specific: location, date, the licensee's name and licence number, any witnesses, and copies of records, correspondence or photographs that support what you are saying.

channels.name: Massachusetts Department of Early Education and Care (EEC)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses the residential facilities and congregate care programs themselves, along with foster care and adoption placement agencies - around 9,000 programs in all - and takes complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: The residential program. EEC also takes reports of care being provided without a licence at all.
channels.how: Call the EEC regional office for the area the program is in. There is a separate online form for reporting unlicensed care.
channels.note: If the complaint involves suspected abuse or neglect rather than a licensing breach, EEC tells you to file a 51A with DCF first.

channels.name: Massachusetts Child-at-Risk Hotline (51A report)
channels.what_it_can_do: The 24-hour line for reporting suspected child abuse or neglect to the Department of Children and Families. A report here is what Massachusetts calls a 51A.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Massachusetts program.
channels.how: Call the hotline. Every other agency in the state will tell you to do this first where abuse or neglect is alleged.

channels.name: Massachusetts Office of the Child Advocate
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office overseeing every child-serving state agency in Massachusetts. It publishes a resource guide naming which agency does what, and takes concerns about how the system has handled a child.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the agencies rather than licensing or prosecuting a program.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person who has reported to a Massachusetts agency and got nowhere.

channels.name: Disability Law Center (Massachusetts)
channels.what_it_can_do: Massachusetts's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Massachusetts program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The SOL for civil CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against any defendant is age 53, with revival up to age 53 against perpetrators only, and a revival 7-year discovery rule against all defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for many sex abuse felonies and an SOL of 6 years from the offense for all remaining felonies and misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM offenses is age 22.

states.note: Michigan puts abuse in a child caring institution through the same centralised intake line as any other child abuse report, and its own guidance says a child can make that call themselves. Reports are then passed to whoever should investigate - law enforcement, or the licensing bureau. Licensing the facility and licensing the therapist are separate departments: MDHHS for the institution, LARA for the clinician.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment; three years for negligence and other personal injury claims.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: If the injured person was under 18 when the claim arose, they have until one year after turning 18 (their 19th birthday) to sue, even if the normal period has run; if the normal period ends later, that later date applies.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: For a personal-injury claim against the State of Michigan, a written claim or notice of intent must be filed with the Court of Claims clerk within 6 months of the event.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Six years from the crime for child abuse in any degree. The clock does not wait until the child turns 18.
items.citation: Mich. Comp. Laws § 767.24(10); Mich. Comp. Laws § 750.136b

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Six years from the crime for felonious assault and assault with intent to do great bodily harm; ten years for assault with intent to commit murder. Misdemeanor assault and battery also appears to fall under the six-year catch-all.

channels.name: Michigan LARA, Bureau of Professional Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints against counselors, marriage and family therapists, psychologists, social workers and other health professionals, assigns an investigator, gathers documents and interviews the professional complained about.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: If the documents and interviews do not establish a violation, the investigation ends and the file is closed.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed mental health professional in Michigan. Anyone can file.
channels.how: Complete the Bureau's complaint form and send it in. It asks whether any civil action or police report is pending, and whether you would be willing to testify at an administrative hearing.

channels.name: Michigan MDHHS, Division of Child Welfare Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child caring institutions, children's foster homes and child placing agencies in Michigan, and investigates licensing complaints against them.
channels.who_to_report: The facility - how it is run, staffed and supervised, as distinct from a specific allegation of abuse, which goes to centralised intake.
channels.how: Use the Division's online complaint form, or its complaint page.

channels.name: Michigan Centralized Intake for Abuse and Neglect
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour line for abuse or neglect of any child or adult, including abuse of a child in a child caring institution, a juvenile court operated facility or a children's foster home. Reports are passed to whoever should investigate - law enforcement, or the licensing bureau.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Michigan program. Michigan says explicitly that anyone can report, including a child.
channels.how: Call, at any hour.

channels.name: Disability Rights Michigan
channels.what_it_can_do: Michigan's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Michigan program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: The civil SOL for CSA claims is age 28 with a 3-year discovery rule.
Trafficking: the civil SOL for trafficking claims is age 28.
CSAM: The civil SOL for CSAM claims is age 19.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for first degree criminal sexual conduct, while the SOL is either age 21, 25, or 28 for other crimes, with a DNA rule.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM is the later of 10 years from the offense or age 21.

states.note: Minnesota keeps a separate board for each profession, so check which licence the person holds before you file. Two things are worth knowing. Any person may voluntarily report a child who is being abused, or who has been abused in the past three years - that lookback is stated in the state's own guidance. And a maltreatment investigation by the Office of Health Facility Complaints ends in a narrative report that is shared with law enforcement, prosecutors and the licensing boards of everyone involved, so one report can reach several places at once.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Negligence claims (for example, a program's negligent supervision) have six years.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock is paused while the injured person is under 18, but the extra time is capped at one year after turning 18. In practice a child's claim must be filed by the later of the normal deadline or the 19th birthday.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Written notice of the claim must be given within 180 days after the injury is discovered: to the attorney general for claims against the state, or to the city or county governing body for claims against a municipality.
items.citation: Minn. Stat. § 3.736, subd. 5; Minn. Stat. § 466.05, subd. 1

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Three years from the crime for malicious punishment of a child, child endangerment, or assault on a child. The clock does not wait until the child turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Three years from the crime for felony assault (first through third degree) and for misdemeanor assault.

channels.name: Minnesota Board of Behavioral Health and Therapy
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors and alcohol and drug counselors in Minnesota. Its reach covers licensees, temporary permit holders, applicants, and people practising without a licence or claiming to hold one of its licences.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It does not licence every mental health profession. Psychologists, social workers and marriage and family therapists each have their own board.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor or alcohol and drug counselor, or somebody claiming to be one.
channels.how: Download the Board's complaint form and complete it. Complaints must be in writing, and can go by post, email or fax.

channels.name: Minnesota Board of Psychology
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in Minnesota.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist.
channels.how: File through the Board's complaints page.

channels.name: Minnesota Board of Marriage and Family Therapy
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines marriage and family therapists in Minnesota.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed marriage and family therapist.
channels.how: File through the Board's complaints page.

channels.name: Minnesota Board of Social Work
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers in Minnesota.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed social worker.
channels.how: Contact the Board for its complaint process.

channels.name: Minnesota Office of Health Facility Complaints (OHFC)
channels.what_it_can_do: The Department of Health's lead investigative agency under the Maltreatment of Minors Act as well as the Vulnerable Adults Act. It investigates complaints against facilities the Department licenses and produces a narrative report finding maltreatment substantiated, inconclusive or unsubstantiated.
channels.who_to_report: A facility licensed by the Minnesota Department of Health.
channels.how: File a complaint against the facility through the Office's complaint page.
channels.note: Its finished report is shared with law enforcement, medical examiners, criminal prosecutors and the licensing boards of everyone involved in the incident. One report can therefore reach several channels without you filing again.

channels.name: Minnesota child maltreatment reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a child protection response. Reports go to the child protection agency in the county or Tribal Nation where the child lives, and intake screeners decide the response path.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Minnesota program. Any person may report voluntarily if they know or suspect a child is being abused or neglected, or has been in the past three years.
channels.how: Contact the county or Tribal Nation child protection agency. If a child is in immediate danger, call 911. Mandated reporters must report within 24 hours and follow up in writing within 72.

channels.name: Minnesota Disability Law Center
channels.what_it_can_do: Minnesota's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Minnesota program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no civil SOL for CSA claims against any defendant.
Trafficking: There is no civil SOL for trafficking claims that fall under the CSA statute. Remaining trafficking claims have an SOL of age 24 under the general personal injury SOL.
CSAM: The civil SOL is age 24 for CSAM claims.
criminal: CSA: In Minnesota, there is no SOL for criminal sexual conduct and prostitution. The SOL for other felonies and misdemeanors is 3 years from the offense.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for sex trafficking.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is 3 years from the offense.

states.note: Mississippi sets the highest bar of any state here for complaining about a clinician: the complaint must be written, signed under oath and notarised, on the Board's own form, and it must name the specific statute or rule you say was broken and the dates of what happened. Anonymous complaints are not investigated at all. Worth preparing properly rather than sending something that will be returned.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Only one year from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Negligence and other personal injury claims have three years.
items.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-35; Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-49

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not start until the injured person is no longer a minor, and in Mississippi a minor is anyone under 21 for this purpose. So an assault or battery claim can be brought until the 22nd birthday, and a negligence claim until the 24th. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.
items.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 15-1-59; Miss. Code Ann. § 1-3-27

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Under the Mississippi Tort Claims Act, suit must be filed within one year of the conduct, and a written notice of claim must be served on the government's chief executive officer at least 90 days before suing; minors get the year after their disability ends.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: No time limit for felonious abuse or battery of a child. Misdemeanor child abuse or neglect must be charged within two years.
items.citation: Miss. Code Ann. § 99-1-5(1)(a); Miss. Code Ann. § 97-5-39(2)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: No time limit for aggravated assault. Simple assault and other offenses not listed: two years.

channels.name: Mississippi Board of Examiners for Social Workers and Marriage and Family Therapists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers and marriage and family therapists in Mississippi, and publishes its disciplinary actions. Any person, firm, corporation, board member or public officer may complain.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It will not investigate an anonymous complaint, and it will only formally address one that arrives in writing on its form.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed social worker or marriage and family therapist in Mississippi.
channels.how: Use the Board's official complaint form. It must be in writing, signed under oath and notarised, must specify the statute or rule allegedly violated, and must set out the acts or omissions and the dates they happened. Post the completed notarised form to the Board.
channels.mail: MSBOESWMFT, P.O. Box 4508, Jackson, MS 39296-4508

channels.name: Mississippi Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour report line run by the Department of Child Protection Services, for abuse, neglect, exploitation and human trafficking. Staff of residential care facilities and group homes licensed by the Department count as persons responsible for the care of children, so their conduct falls squarely within what this line takes.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Mississippi program.
channels.how: Call the hotline, or report online through the Department's site.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Mississippi State Department of Health, Child Care Facilities Licensure
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses child care facilities in Mississippi and runs a dedicated licensure complaint line, separate from the child abuse hotline.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed facility, where the issue is a licensing breach rather than abuse.
channels.how: Call the licensure complaint hotline.
channels.phone_note: Child Care Facilities Licensure complaint line, toll free.

channels.name: Disability Rights Mississippi
channels.what_it_can_do: Mississippi's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Mississippi program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims is age 24 against all defendants, with a discovery rule.
criminal: CSA: In Mississippi, there is no SOL for many CSA felonies and an SOL of 5 years for sexual battery or fondling of a vulnerable person. For the remaining felonies and misdemeanors, the SOL is 2 years after the offense.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM offenses.

states.note: Missouri matters to this industry for a particular reason: for decades religious residential facilities operated here entirely outside licensing. HB 557, signed in July 2021, did not licence them, but it did require every license-exempt facility to register with the state and to run background checks on everyone with access to children. So a Missouri program may be licensed, registered-but-exempt, or operating in breach of the notification law - and which one it is changes who you report to.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Negligence and other personal injury claims have five years.
items.citation: Mo. Rev. Stat. § 516.140; Mo. Rev. Stat. § 516.120(4)

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: If the injured person was under 21 when the claim arose, the normal period starts when they turn 21: assault or battery by the 23rd birthday, negligence by the 26th. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Missouri keeps sovereign immunity for the state and local governments except for injuries from vehicle operation and dangerous property conditions, so most abuse claims cannot be brought against the government entity itself; no general notice-of-claim statute was found.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Abuse or neglect of a child is usually a class D felony, which must be charged within three years of the crime; if it caused serious physical or emotional injury (class B), also three years. If the child died (class A), there is no limit. The clock does not wait until the child turns 18.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Three years from the crime for felony assault (first degree class B, second degree). No limit for first degree assault that inflicts great bodily harm or targets a 'special victim' (class A). Misdemeanor assault: one year.

channels.name: Missouri Division of Professional Registration
channels.what_it_can_do: Houses the separate committees that license psychologists, professional counselors, social workers and physicians, and investigates complaints about them. Each committee can discipline the licence it issued.
channels.who_to_report: Any licensed clinician in Missouri. One form covers all of them; the committee it goes to depends on the licence.
channels.how: All the committees use the same complaint form, number 375-0195. Download it, fill it in, and send it to the committee that issued the licence.
channels.phone_note: Professional Counselors. Psychologists 573-751-0099; Social Workers 573-751-0885; Healing Arts, for physicians and psychiatrists, 573-751-0098.
channels.mail: Division of Professional Registration, P.O. Box 1335, Jefferson City, MO 65102-1335
channels.note: Each committee publishes its own disciplinary actions, so you can check whether a name has come up before.

channels.name: Missouri Children's Division, residential licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses residential care facilities and child placing agencies for children and youth, runs the background check requirements, and holds the register of license-exempt facilities. Unless the law specifically exempts them, private agencies providing residential treatment for children must be licensed by the Division.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It does not licence the exempt facilities, only record that they exist. An exempt program is still bound by the background check rules in 13 CSR 35-71.015 and by the duty to notify the Division that it is operating.
channels.who_to_report: The facility. A program that never told the Division it exists is itself a violation worth reporting.
channels.how: Contact the Children's Division. Its residential licensing pages set out what a licensed and a license-exempt facility each have to do.

channels.name: Missouri Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect in Missouri, staffed around the clock. A report starts a Children's Division response and can bring in law enforcement.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Missouri program right now.
channels.how: Call the hotline, or use the Online System for Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting (OSCR).
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, every day. Relay Missouri 1-800-735-2466 voice, 1-800-735-2966 text.

channels.name: Missouri Attorney General, Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates and prosecutes abuse and neglect of residents in Medicaid-funded facilities, alongside Medicaid provider fraud.
channels.who_to_report: A Medicaid-funded Missouri program where a young person was abused or neglected.
channels.how: Call the toll-free line, use the online resident abuse complaint form, email or write.
channels.mail: Missouri Attorney General's Office, Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, P.O. Box 899, Jefferson City, MO 65102

channels.name: Missouri Protection and Advocacy Services
channels.what_it_can_do: Missouri's federally mandated P&A. Authority to investigate abuse and neglect where a person with a disability receives services, with a right of access to the facility, plus free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Missouri program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims is age 31 against perpetrators, and age twenty-six against other defendants, with a discovery rule.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for felony and misdemeanor CSA offenses.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM violations.

states.note: Montana licenses these programs under their own category - Private Alternative Adolescent Residential or Outdoor Programs - so there is a regulator whose job is specifically this industry. Oversight moved in 2019: the legislature dissolved the old PAARP board at the Department of Labor and gave licensing to DPHHS, which has since revoked a program's licence outright. Complaints to the Licensure Bureau are always anonymous, and the corrective actions it imposes are published.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for assault, battery or false imprisonment. Negligence and other personal injury claims have three years.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The time while the injured person is a minor does not count, so the clock starts at 18: assault or battery claims by the 20th birthday, negligence claims by the 21st. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: A claim against the State must first be presented in writing to the Department of Administration, which has 120 days to decide (the deadline to sue pauses for those 120 days); claims against a county or city are filed with its clerk. The ordinary 2- or 3-year periods still apply.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Five years from the crime for felony assault on a minor (victim under 14, offender an adult) or other felony child abuse. Misdemeanor child endangerment: one year. The clock does not wait until the child turns 18.
items.citation: Mont. Code Ann. § 45-1-205(2); Mont. Code Ann. § 45-5-212

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Five years from the crime for aggravated assault or any other felony. Misdemeanor assault: one year.

channels.name: Montana Board of Behavioral Health (Department of Labor and Industry)
channels.what_it_can_do: The Department and its licensing boards take action against unprofessional, incompetent or unlawful practice, up to discipline of the licence. The Board of Behavioral Health covers mental health counselors, licensed professional counselors, addiction counselors and social workers; psychologists have their own board, and the same complaint route serves both.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: To bring formal charges the Department needs evidence in the form of a document or a statement - a complaint with nothing behind it will not get far.
channels.who_to_report: Anyone holding a Montana behavioral health or psychology licence. The Department's licence search shows current status and any disciplinary history.
channels.how: Use the online licence complaint form. There is a downloadable paper form as an alternative, and an FAQ written for complainants rather than licensees.
channels.mail: Board of Behavioral Health, 301 S. Park Avenue, 4th Floor, Helena, MT 59620
channels.note: This board covers the clinician, not the program. A complaint about a facility goes to the DPHHS Licensure Bureau instead, and the Department's own page says so.

channels.name: Montana DPHHS, Quality Assurance Division, Licensure Bureau
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates private alternative adolescent residential and outdoor programs, inspects them, imposes corrective action and can revoke a licence. It has done so: Montana permanently revoked one program's licence and removed the children from another.
channels.who_to_report: The program itself - conditions, staffing, supervision, how it treats the young people in it.
channels.how: Contact the Licensure Bureau by phone or post. The corrective actions it imposes are published on the Bureau's website, so it is worth reading what a program has already been cited for.
channels.mail: DPHHS Licensure Bureau, PO Box 202953, Helena, MT 59620-2953
channels.note: DPHHS states that complaints against the programs it licenses are always kept anonymous.

channels.name: Montana Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline (Centralized Intake)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory intake line for child abuse and neglect. Where a complaint covers both abuse and a licensing breach, the Child and Family Services Division leads the child protection side of the investigation and the Licensure Bureau handles the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Montana program right now. Montana's own rules require the programs themselves to report suspected abuse to this number.
channels.how: Call. It takes reports around the clock.

channels.name: Montana Office of the Child and Family Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office in the Department of Justice that reviews how the child protection system handles a case and publishes its findings. Useful when a report has already been made and nothing happened.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the state's handling rather than investigating the program directly, and it does not licence anybody.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person who reported something and has hit a wall.
channels.how: File a request for assistance online.

channels.name: Disability Rights Montana
channels.what_it_can_do: Montana's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Montana program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims is age 27 against all defendants, with a limited 3-year discovery rule and revival up to age 27.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for felony and misdemeanor CSA offenses.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM offenses.

states.note: Nebraska has an Office of Inspector General of Nebraska Child Welfare that sits in the legislature rather than in the department it scrutinises, and takes complaints directly. That independence matters when the concern is that the agency itself is not acting. Nebraska also says its hotline reports are confidential and are not shared with the family.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Four years for personal injury, including assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence. (Nebraska used to have a one-year limit for assault and battery, but it was removed in 2000.)

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. If you were a minor when hurt, the clock does not start until the disability ends. Nebraska courts read the statute's 'within the age of twenty years' to mean until your 21st birthday, so the four-year limit usually runs to age 25. There is no general extended deadline for physical (non-sexual) child abuse.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: State of Nebraska: a written claim must be filed with the Risk Manager within two years. Counties, cities, school districts and other political subdivisions: a written claim within one year and a lawsuit within two years. For minors these deadlines are tolled under 25-213.
items.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-8,227 (State Tort Claims Act); 13-919 (Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act)

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: For child abuse (felony or misdemeanor) when the child was under 16: seven years from the abuse or seven years from the child's 16th birthday, whichever is later. If the child was 16 or 17, the general limits apply (three years for a felony, 18 months for a misdemeanor).

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Three years from the offense for felony assault (first- and second-degree assault). Misdemeanor (third-degree) assault: 18 months.
items.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. 29-110(1), (2); assault offenses 28-308 to 28-310

channels.name: Nebraska DHHS, Division of Public Health, Office of Investigations
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints against licensed, registered and certified health care professionals in Nebraska, including mental health practitioners and psychologists, for breaches of the Uniform Credentialing Act and the rules governing their practice.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed mental health practitioner or psychologist in Nebraska.
channels.how: Get the reporting form from the Investigations page or by phone. Describe every allegation in detail, give specific dates for each incident, list any witnesses, and attach copies of the documents that bear on it.
channels.note: A licensed professional has to report their own misdemeanour or felony conviction, or discipline elsewhere, to this office within 30 days - so it may already hold a history.

channels.name: Nebraska DHHS Children's Services Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses Residential Child-Caring Agencies and Child-Placing Agencies in Nebraska, and investigates every allegation of a licensing violation in a children and youth care facility.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed residential child-caring agency.
channels.how: Email or write to Children's Services Licensing.
channels.mail: DHHS Children's Services Licensing, PO Box 94986, Lincoln, NE 68509

channels.name: Nebraska Child Abuse and Neglect Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide report line for suspected child abuse and neglect.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Nebraska program.
channels.how: Call, or report through the online hotline system.
channels.note: Reports are confidential and are not shared with the family. A Child and Family Services Specialist may contact you during the assessment, and you can ask to stay anonymous. Online, the reporter's information stays confidential unless a court or a law enforcement agency with jurisdiction requests it.

channels.name: Office of Inspector General of Nebraska Child Welfare
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office in the Nebraska legislature, outside the department it oversees, taking complaints about the child welfare system and the facilities in it.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It scrutinises the system rather than licensing or prosecuting a program itself.
channels.who_to_report: Anyone who believes Nebraska's child welfare system, or a facility within it, has failed a child - particularly where a report to the department has gone nowhere.
channels.how: File through the Office's own complaint page.

channels.name: Disability Rights Nebraska
channels.what_it_can_do: Nebraska's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Nebraska program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no civil SOL for child sexual assault claims against perpetrators. The SOL is age 33 for child sexual assault claims against all other defendants and age 25 for all other CSA claims.
Trafficking: The civil SOL for trafficking claims is age 25.
CSAM: The civil SOL for CSAM claims is age 25.
criminal: CSA: There is no criminal SOL for many CSA crimes, and the SOL for lesser degrees of those offenses is age 25 or age 23, with an 18-month SOL for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for felony trafficking crimes.
CSAM: There is no SOL for felony CSAM offenses.

states.note: Nevada has no single child abuse hotline. Clark County and Washoe County each run their own, and the Division of Child and Family Services covers everywhere else - and in those rural counties, out of hours, the Division tells you to call local law enforcement instead. Nevada's board websites were also mid-reorganisation when this was checked, and several published complaint forms had gone; where that is the case the phone number and address below came from the board's own live page, and it is worth asking them to send you the current form.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years. The same two-year limit covers assault, battery and false imprisonment, and personal injury caused by negligence.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: Yes. Time while you are under 18 does not count, so the two years usually run to your 20th birthday. Time spent in the State's custodial care (for example foster care or a state placement begun before 18) also does not count, unless the person is imprisoned, paroled or on probation. No general extended period for physical (non-sexual) child abuse.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: A tort claim against the State of Nevada is filed with the Attorney General, and against a county, city or other political subdivision with its governing body, within two years; filing that administrative claim is not a precondition to suing, and the lawsuit itself follows the normal two-year limit.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Three years from the offense for felony child abuse or neglect. For physical abuse there is no pause until the child turns 18; the longer child-victim deadlines (age 36 or 43) apply only to sexual abuse and sex trafficking. If the abuse was committed in a secret manner, the three years start when it is discovered.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Three years from the offense for felony battery or assault. Gross misdemeanors: two years. Misdemeanor battery or assault: one year.

channels.name: Nevada Board of Examiners for Marriage and Family Therapists and Clinical Professional Counselors
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints against Nevada marriage and family therapists, clinical professional counselors, their interns, and anyone else under its jurisdiction including allegations of unlicensed practice, and disciplines licences.
channels.who_to_report: An LMFT or CPC in Nevada, an intern working under one, or somebody practising without the licence.
channels.how: The complaint must be in writing and signed by you, and posted with your supporting documents. Ask the Board for its current complaint form.
channels.phone_note: Walk-in, phone and email hours are Tuesday to Thursday, 9am to 4pm only.
channels.mail: Board of Examiners for Marriage and Family Therapists and Clinical Professional Counselors, 500 N. Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 201, Las Vegas, NV 89107

channels.name: Nevada Board of Psychological Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Reviews and disciplines complaints against licensed psychologists in Nevada.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist.
channels.how: Complete the Board's complaint form, and the Release of Psychological Records form where it applies, with as much detail and supporting documentation as you can. Complaints cannot be taken by phone - they must be in writing.
channels.mail: Nevada Board of Psychological Examiners, 3080 South Durango Drive, Suite 102, Las Vegas, NV 89117

channels.name: Nevada Board of Examiners for Social Workers
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers in Nevada, including licensed clinical social workers. It calls the process filing an accusation of wrongdoing.
channels.who_to_report: An LCSW or other licensed social worker.
channels.how: File an accusation of wrongdoing through the Board's consumer page, which also sets out the disciplinary laws and regulations it works to.
