channels.phone_note: Toll free, Monday to Friday 8:00am to 4:30pm.
channels.mail: Tennessee Health Facilities Commission, Andrew Jackson Building, 9th Floor, 502 Deaderick Street, Nashville, TN 37243
channels.note: The online Public Records and Complaints portal opened to the public in July 2025 and is the quickest route.

channels.name: Tennessee DCS, Office of Child Welfare Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates Tennessee's non-clinical residential programs for children and youth, including private foster care programs, runaway houses and maternity homes, and takes complaints about them. Its board of review weighs the safety and best interests of the children, the training and character of the staff, and whether caregivers will actually protect children from harm.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It does not licence a facility providing clinical treatment; that is the Health Facilities Commission, or the Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services.
channels.who_to_report: A non-clinical residential program, or a program you believe is operating without the licence it needs.
channels.how: Email the licensing office with the details, or call the child care complaint hotline.

channels.name: Tennessee Child Abuse Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect, run by the Department of Children's Services.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Tennessee program. Tennessee Code 37-1-403 makes everyone in the state a mandated reporter.
channels.how: Call, or use the secure online referral portal. At weekends the phone line redirects you to the portal, so use it directly then.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours on weekdays. From 11pm Central Friday to 11pm Central Sunday the call is redirected to the online portal.

channels.name: Disability Rights Tennessee
channels.what_it_can_do: Tennessee's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Tennessee program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against all defendants is age 33 with a 3-year discovery rule.
criminal: There is no SOL for all CSA felonies and many misdemeanors, including trafficking and CSAM, but admissible and credible evidence corroborating the charges is required where a victim is now over age 43, was abused between ages 13 and 17, and did not report the abuse.

states.note: Texas folds the psychology, counseling, social work and marriage and family therapy boards into one council, BHEC, so one form covers most therapists; psychiatrists are separate, under the Medical Board. Texas is also one of the few states that publishes its filing deadline plainly, and it is longer than most: five years, and longer still for sexual misconduct.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years for personal injury, which covers assault, battery, negligence and false imprisonment.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: If you were under 18 when you were hurt, the time before your 18th birthday does not count. The two years start at 18, so the deadline is your 20th birthday.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: The Texas Tort Claims Act does not cover assault, battery, false imprisonment or other intentional harm, so those claims generally cannot be brought against a state or local government program at all; a survivor may need to sue the staff or a private contractor instead. For negligence claims it does cover, notice is due within six months of the incident unless the government already knew of the injury.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Felony injury to a child and felony abandoning or endangering a child can be charged until 10 years after the victim's 18th birthday (the victim's 28th birthday).

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Five years for aggravated assault. Most other felonies: three years. Misdemeanor assault: two years (three for family violence).

channels.name: Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council (BHEC)
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates and prosecutes professional misconduct by psychologists, psychological associates, licensed specialists in school psychology, professional counselors, marriage and family therapists and social workers. It can discipline a licence up to revoking it.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It will not open an investigation at all unless the complaint arrives on its own form, and the whole complaint file is confidential by statute, so you cannot later obtain the investigation report.
channels.who_to_report: A therapist holding any Texas behavioral health licence. If the person is a psychiatrist, use the Medical Board instead.
channels.how: Fill in the Council's complaint form and email it to Enforcement@bhec.texas.gov or post it. Send supporting material with it; the Council asks for it.
channels.mail: Texas Behavioral Health Executive Council, 1801 Congress Ave., Ste. 7.300, Austin, TX 78701
channels.deadline: Generally five years from the date services ended. For sexual misconduct, seven years from the date services ended or five years from the client's 18th birthday, whichever is later.
channels.note: The licensee is sent a copy of the complaint including your name, unless you file anonymously. File anonymously and you will not be told the outcome. The Council aims to resolve complaints in six to twelve months.

channels.name: Texas Medical Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines physicians, which in this industry means the psychiatrist who signed off the medication or the medical director whose name is on the program.
channels.who_to_report: A doctor, including a psychiatrist. Not a therapist or counselor - those go to BHEC.
channels.how: File through the online complaint portal, or call the hotline and follow the prompts to be sent a paper form. It must be in writing.
channels.phone_note: Complaint hotline. Main line 512-305-7100; help with the online portal on 512-305-7030.
channels.note: The Board does not accept anonymous complaints, but your identity is confidential by law once you file.

channels.name: Texas HHS Complaint and Incident Intake
channels.what_it_can_do: The single intake point for complaints about any provider Texas HHS regulates, including allegations of abuse, neglect and exploitation by the provider. It routes them to the regulatory division that can inspect the facility and act on its licence.
channels.who_to_report: The program itself: how it is run, how it is staffed, what it does to the young people in it.
channels.how: Report online through the Texas Unified Licensure Information Portal (TULIP), or call. Email is accepted for complaints, though not for urgent ones.
channels.note: For an inpatient substance use facility specifically, HHSC Health Care Regulation has its own line on 1-888-973-0022.

channels.name: Texas Abuse Hotline (Department of Family and Protective Services)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect in Texas, including abuse of children in child care facilities and treatment centers, which DFPS investigates through its Child Care Investigations division.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Texas program right now. If the danger is immediate, call 911 first.
channels.how: Call the hotline, or report through the secure website, which promises a response within 24 hours. DFPS will not take a report by email and cannot accept photos or recordings that way.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, every day, from anywhere in the country.

channels.name: Texas Attorney General, Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
channels.what_it_can_do: Criminally investigates abuse and neglect of patients in facilities that take Medicaid, along with misappropriation of a patient's money or property, and Medicaid provider fraud. It can bring criminal charges.
channels.who_to_report: A Medicaid-funded program where a young person was abused or neglected, or where money or property went missing.
channels.how: Call the unit. It has field offices in Austin, Corpus Christi, El Paso, Grand Prairie, Houston, Lubbock, Pharr and San Antonio.
channels.mail: Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, Office of the Attorney General, PO Box 12548, Austin, TX 78711-2548

channels.name: Disability Rights Texas
channels.what_it_can_do: Texas's federally mandated Protection and Advocacy agency. It can investigate abuse and neglect where a person with a disability receives services, has a right of access to the facility, and provides free legal advocacy. It publishes its own guide to complaining about inpatient mental health services.
channels.who_to_report: A Texas program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Apply for help through the website or the intake line.

channels.name: Texas HHS Ombudsman for Behavioral Health
channels.what_it_can_do: Helps resolve a complaint about behavioral health services and makes sure it reaches the body that oversees whoever is paying for the care. It publishes a rights handbook for people receiving mental health services, including a version written for teenagers.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It is a route through the system rather than an enforcement body. An immediate risk of abuse goes to the Abuse Hotline, not here.
channels.who_to_report: Someone who cannot get behavioral health care, or cannot get a complaint about it taken seriously.
channels.how: Call, or submit online.
channels.phone_note: 8am to 5pm, Monday to Friday. Relay Texas on 711 or 1-800-735-2989.
channels.mail: Texas Health and Human Services Commission, Ombudsman for Behavioral Health, P.O. Box 13247, Austin, TX 78711-3247

civil: CSA: The civil SOL for CSA claims against all defendants is age 48 with a very narrow discovery rule.
Trafficking: The civil SOL for trafficking claims against all defendants is age 48.
CSAM: The civil SOL for CSAM claims is age 20.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for some CSA offenses. The SOL is age 38 for sexual performance, and the SOL is 3 years from the offense for any remaining felonies and two years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking offenses.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is 7 years from the offense.

states.note: Utah licenses every mental health profession through one division, DOPL, so a complaint about a therapist, a psychologist, a counselor or a psychiatrist all start in the same place. It is also one of the few states with an ombuds office written specifically for young people in residential programs, and that office takes calls from the youth themselves.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Four years from the injury for physical injury, including assault, battery and negligence. False imprisonment has a shorter deadline: one year.
items.citation: Utah Code § 78B-2-307(4) (four-year catch-all); Utah Code § 78B-2-302(4) (one year for false imprisonment)

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18. For someone injured as a child, the deadline (four years, or one year for false imprisonment) starts at 18. Utah has no longer deadline for physical abuse of a child. The longer child abuse deadline in § 78B-2-308 covers sexual abuse only.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: To sue the state, a county, a city or their employees, you must file a written notice of claim within one year after the claim arises. You must then file the lawsuit within two years after the claim arises, and not sooner than 60 days after the notice.
items.citation: Utah Code §§ 63G-7-401, 63G-7-402, 63G-7-403 (Governmental Immunity Act of Utah)

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Four years from the abuse for felony child abuse. Misdemeanor child abuse: two years. Utah does not pause the criminal clock until the child turns 18 for non-sexual physical abuse. Child abuse homicide can be charged at any time.
items.citation: Utah Code § 76-1-302(1); Utah Code § 76-1-301(2)(e) (child abuse homicide, no limit)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Four years from the assault for felony (aggravated) assault. Misdemeanor assault: two years.

channels.name: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL)
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates licensed professionals and can discipline, restrict, suspend or revoke a licence. It licenses psychologists, clinical social workers, clinical mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, substance use disorder counselors and physicians, so one complaint form covers whichever kind of clinician it was.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says in writing that it will not act as your attorney, will not recover money for you, and cannot investigate for the benefit of your own lawsuit.
channels.who_to_report: A named clinician who holds or held a Utah licence. It also takes complaints about unlicensed people practising as though they were licensed, which is worth knowing in an industry that leans on unlicensed staff.
channels.how: File through the online complaint service, or download the PDF form and mail it. Complete every section; write N/A where one does not apply.
channels.phone_note: Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm Mountain, except state holidays.
channels.mail: Utah Division of Professional Licensing, P.O. Box 146741, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-6741
channels.note: Complaints are not public record under Utah law. DOPL publishes the disciplinary actions that result, so you can check whether anything came of an earlier one.

channels.name: Utah Office of Licensing, Division of Licensing and Background Checks (DLBC)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and inspects the residential treatment programs, therapeutic schools and outdoor youth programs themselves. It sets the health and safety standards, inspects against them, and can require corrective action, impose civil money penalties, or act against the licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It regulates the program, not the individual therapist - that is DOPL - and it does not investigate the abuse allegation itself, which goes to DCFS.
channels.who_to_report: The facility: staffing levels, restraint and seclusion practice, conditions, supervision, anything that is a standards problem rather than one person's conduct.
channels.how: Contact the Office of Licensing directly. Utah publishes its inspection findings, so it is worth reading what has already been cited before you call.
channels.phone_note: Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm, except state holidays.
channels.mail: Division of Licensing and Background Checks, 195 North 1950 West, Salt Lake City, UT 84116

channels.name: Utah Division of Child and Family Services child abuse hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory intake point for child abuse and neglect in Utah. A report here starts a CPS investigation and can bring in law enforcement.
channels.who_to_report: A child currently at a program in Utah who is being abused or neglected, or who is in a situation likely to result in it.
channels.how: Call the 24/7 intake line, or use the online reporting form. Give names and ages, what happened, any injuries you saw, and dates.
channels.deadline: No deadline on making a report.
channels.note: Under Utah Code 80-2-601 anyone who believes a child is being abused must report it; failure to report can be a crime. Reporters acting in good faith are protected from civil and criminal liability. If DCFS itself mishandles the report, the independent Child Protection Ombudsman takes complaints about DCFS on 801-538-4589.

channels.name: Utah Attorney General, Medicaid Fraud and Patient Abuse Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Criminally investigates and prosecutes both Medicaid provider fraud and the abuse, neglect or exploitation of patients, where the abuse happened in a health care facility or any setting where a provider is paid by Medicaid. This is a prosecutor's office, not a licensing body: it is the channel that can put somebody in front of a criminal court.
channels.who_to_report: A program paid by Medicaid where a young person was abused, neglected or exploited, or where the billing does not match the care that was given.
channels.how: Call or email the division directly, or use the Attorney General's online report form.

channels.name: Utah Youth in Care (Congregate Care) Ombuds
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office inside DHHS for young people in residential programs, therapeutic schools and outdoor youth programs. It listens, advocates, conducts independent reviews, works directly with the program, and can open an investigation. It takes calls from a youth still inside a Utah program and from a parent in another state.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It does not investigate abuse or neglect allegations - those go to DCFS - and it does not investigate health and safety standards, which go to the Office of Licensing. It refers them on rather than dropping them. It does not give legal advice.
channels.who_to_report: A young person in a Utah program who feels unheard or unsafe, or a parent who cannot get a straight answer out of the program.
channels.how: Submit the online contact form. You will hear back within three business days, and contact is confidential.
channels.deadline: There is a time limit and the office states it two different ways: the program page says you must make contact within 9 months of the incident, while the contact form says the situation must have occurred within the last 3 months. Treat 3 months as the safe assumption and call if you are outside it.

channels.name: Disability Law Center (Utah's Protection and Advocacy agency)
channels.what_it_can_do: Utah's federally mandated P&A. It investigates abuse and neglect in residential facilities, has a right of access to them, and provides free legal advocacy to eligible clients, including representation in hearings and court. Its published reports on Utah programs have forced state responses.
channels.who_to_report: A Utah program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis. Call and ask if you are not sure whether that applies.
channels.how: Intake by phone, or online through the site. It no longer takes walk-ins, though you can come in to fill in the paperwork.
channels.phone_note: Salt Lake City line 801-363-1347. Video Relay Service available.

civil: There is no civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against perpetrators. The SOL is age 22 against other defendants with a 4-year discovery rule.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for many CSA felonies. The SOL is age 28 for claims involving unlawful sexual activity, and 4 to 8 eight years after the crime is reported for other felonies. The SOL is 2 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking felonies.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is 4 years from the offense.

states.note: Vermont runs one number for both jobs: the Department for Children and Families Centralized Intake Unit takes child abuse reports and complaints about residential treatment programs alike, and Vermont's licensing rules require a residential treatment program to cooperate fully in any investigation of a complaint or allegation about it.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Three years for assault and battery, false imprisonment, and other personal injury including negligence. For personal injury in general, the three years run from when the injury was discovered.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: No time limit to sue over physical abuse as a child that would count as aggravated assault, or over childhood sexual abuse. For other injuries, the three years start at 18.
items.citation: 12 V.S.A. § 522 (childhood sexual or physical abuse); 12 V.S.A. § 551(a) (minority)

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Vermont's state tort claims law has no separate notice-of-claim deadline. However, the state has not waived immunity for assault and battery claims unless insurance covers them, and state employees can be sued personally only for gross negligence or willful misconduct.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Three years from the offense for most non-sexual child abuse and cruelty offenses. Maiming has a 40-year limit, and murder and manslaughter have none. Vermont does not pause the criminal clock until 18 for non-sexual abuse.

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Three years from the offense for aggravated assault and for simple assault. First degree aggravated domestic assault has 11 years, and maiming has 40 years.

channels.name: Vermont Office of Professional Regulation
channels.what_it_can_do: Regulates Vermont's clinical social workers, clinical mental health counselors, psychologists and other allied mental health professions. On a complaint it runs an administrative review to see whether the professional conduct statute covers what you describe, then assigns a committee to investigate and recommend action. Discipline runs from a warning to revoking the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed clinical social worker, clinical mental health counselor or psychologist in Vermont.
channels.how: Call or write to the Director of the Office to obtain a complaint form.
channels.mail: Director, Office of Professional Regulation, Secretary of State's Office, 89 Main Street, 3rd Floor, Montpelier, VT 05620-3402
channels.note: All complaint investigations are confidential.

channels.name: Vermont DCF residential treatment program licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses Vermont's residential treatment programs and investigates complaints against them. Its rules require a licensed program to cooperate fully in the investigation of any complaint or allegation associated with it.
channels.who_to_report: A Vermont residential treatment program.
channels.how: Report to the Centralized Intake Unit, which takes program complaints as well as abuse reports.
channels.phone_note: Centralized Intake Unit. 24 hours a day.

channels.name: Vermont child abuse and neglect hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line, run by the Family Services Division's Centralized Intake Unit, open every hour of every day.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Vermont program.
channels.how: Call.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Disability Rights Vermont
channels.what_it_can_do: Vermont's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Vermont program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: CSA: There is no civil SOL for CSA and claims against all defendants are permanently revived.
Trafficking: The civil SOL for trafficking is age 21.
CSAM: The civil SOL for CSAM is age 21.
criminal: CSA: There is no criminal SOL for aggravated sexual assault or exploitation. The SOL is 40 years from the offense for some CSA crimes, and 3 years from the offense for all other felonies and misdemeanors.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is 40 years from the offense.

states.note: Virginia is blunt about the cost of filing, and it is worth reading before you do. A complaint to the Department of Health Professions cannot be withdrawn once submitted, you cannot get a copy of your own form back afterwards, and Virginia law requires the details to be shared with the licensee you complained about. The Department cannot guarantee anonymity either - if you want to be anonymous, it warns that you must keep your identity out of the form and every document attached to it.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for any personal injury, whether it is assault, battery or negligence. False imprisonment is also two years.
items.citation: Va. Code § 8.01-243(A); Va. Code § 8.01-248 (catch-all for personal actions)

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18. For someone injured as a child, the two years start at 18. Virginia's longer deadline and discovery rule for childhood abuse cover sexual abuse only, not physical abuse.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: For a claim against the state (Commonwealth), file a written notice of claim within one year. The lawsuit must then be filed within 18 months of the notice or two years of the injury. For negligence claims against a county, city or town, the written notice is due within six months. For both, the clock is paused for a child until 18.
items.citation: Va. Code §§ 8.01-195.6, 8.01-195.7 (Virginia Tort Claims Act); Va. Code § 15.2-209 (localities)

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: No time limit for felony child abuse or neglect: Virginia has no statute of limitations for felonies. Misdemeanor offenses generally must be charged within one year.
items.citation: Va. Code § 19.2-8 (limits misdemeanors only); Va. Code § 18.2-371.1 (felony child abuse and neglect)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: No time limit for felony assault (malicious or unlawful wounding and other felonies). Misdemeanor assault and battery must be charged within one year.

channels.name: Virginia Department of Health Professions, Enforcement Division
channels.what_it_can_do: Receives and investigates complaints for all thirteen of Virginia's licensing and regulatory boards, including the Board of Counseling, the Board of Social Work and the Board of Psychology, and the boards discipline the licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It has no authority to make a licensee return money or provide any other personal remedy. It cannot give you a copy of your complaint form once submitted, and the complaint cannot be withdrawn.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor, social worker or psychologist in Virginia. Identify them by full name and licence type.
channels.how: Use the online complaint form, or return the Word or PDF form to the Enforcement Division by email, fax, post or in person.
channels.mail: Virginia Department of Health Professions, Enforcement Division, Perimeter Center, 9960 Mayland Drive, Suite 300, Henrico, VA 23233-1463
channels.note: Anonymity cannot be guaranteed. If you mean to file anonymously, the Department warns you must leave any identifying information out of both the form and every supporting document - naming yourself anywhere means you are not anonymous.

channels.name: Virginia Department of Social Services, Division of Licensing Programs
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and inspects children's residential facilities in Virginia and takes complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed children's residential facility. A facility providing behavioral health treatment may instead be licensed by the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services, which runs its own Office of Licensing.
channels.how: Use the online complaint form or call the licensing line.

channels.name: Virginia DBHDS Office of Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates behavioral health and developmental services providers in Virginia, including residential treatment programs, and investigates complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A program licensed to provide mental health or substance use treatment, as distinct from a children's residential facility licensed by Social Services.
channels.how: Contact the Office of Licensing through its contact page, which lists the specialist for each region and service type.

channels.name: Virginia Child Protective Services Hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour line for reporting suspected child abuse or neglect, which routes the report to the local department that investigates.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Virginia program.
channels.how: Call. Virginia says you do not have to give your name, and you do not have to provide evidence to make a report.

channels.name: disAbility Law Center of Virginia
channels.what_it_can_do: Virginia's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Virginia program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and some CSAM claims is age 38 with a 20-year discovery rule against all defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no criminal SOL for any felonies, including CSA. The SOL for misdemeanors is age 23 or age 19, depending on the age difference between the victim and the offender.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking felonies.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM felonies.

states.note: Washington is unusually clear about what its health complaint system will and will not take on: unprofessional conduct, a provider unable to practise safely, and unlicensed practice, but not scheduling, personality conflicts or billing. It also has an independent Office of the Family and Children's Ombuds, which exists to look at how the state itself handled a child's case.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years for assault, battery and false imprisonment. Three years for negligence and other personal injury.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18. For someone injured as a child, the two or three years start at 18. Washington's special childhood abuse law covers sexual abuse only, not physical abuse.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Before suing the state, file a claim form with the Office of Risk Management. For a county, city or other local government, file the claim with its designated agent. Either way the claim must be filed within the normal deadline, and you must wait 60 days before suing. The deadline is paused during those 60 days.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Three years from the offense for felony assault of a child and other non-sexual child abuse felonies. Homicide by abuse can be charged at any time. Washington does not pause the criminal clock until 18 for non-sexual physical abuse.
items.citation: RCW 9A.04.080(1)(j); RCW 9A.04.080(1)(a)(ii) (homicide by abuse, no limit)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Three years from the offense for felony assault (first, second and third degree). Gross misdemeanor assault: two years. Simple misdemeanor: one year.

channels.name: Washington State Department of Health, Health Systems Quality Assurance
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines mental health counselors, marriage and family therapists, social workers and psychologists, and investigates three kinds of complaint: unprofessional conduct, a provider whose mental or physical condition means they cannot practise with reasonable skill and safety, and practice without a valid Washington credential.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says plainly it may not be able to help with complaints unrelated to patient safety - scheduling problems, personality conflicts, disputes over bills or insurance.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed mental health professional in Washington, or somebody practising without a credential. Physicians go to the Washington Medical Commission instead.
channels.how: Use the Department's complaint forms. The complaint process page explains what happens to it afterwards.
channels.phone_note: Health Systems Quality Assurance customer service.

channels.name: Washington State Department of Health, facility complaints
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes and investigates complaints about the health care facilities the Department licenses, through a process separate from the one for individual providers.
channels.who_to_report: A DOH-licensed facility, including behavioral health agencies.
channels.how: Use the facility complaint process and the Department's complaint forms.

channels.name: Washington child abuse and neglect hotline (End Harm)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statewide 24-hour line, which connects you to the local office that will take the report. It also takes concerns about a licensed facility, and about unlicensed care.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Washington program, and any concern about how a licensed facility is treating children.
channels.how: Call. A DCYF licensor starts acting on a referral within five working days, and a complaint is usually inspected and resolved within 45 days.
channels.phone_note: 1-866-END-HARM. 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
channels.note: For a complaint about DCYF itself rather than about a program, Constituent Relations takes those on 1-800-723-4831.

channels.name: Washington Office of the Family and Children's Ombuds
channels.what_it_can_do: An independent office that reviews how the state's child protection and child welfare system handled a case, and publishes where it finds fault.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It examines the state's conduct rather than licensing or prosecuting a program.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person whose report to a Washington agency went nowhere.

channels.name: Disability Rights Washington
channels.what_it_can_do: Washington's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Washington program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and some CSAM claims is age 21 with a 3-year discovery rule against all defendants.
criminal: CSA: There is no criminal SOL for many CSA crimes. The SOL is age 30 for other felonies and age 20 for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking is 10 years from the offense, while the SOL for commercial sex abuse is age 30.
CSAM: There is no SOL for some CSAM crimes. Other CSAM offenses have an SOL of 3 years from the offense.

states.note: West Virginia funnels every report of suspected abuse or neglect - of children and of vulnerable adults alike - through one Centralized Intake, staffed every hour of every day of the year. Its counseling board is candid about the limit on what a complaint can achieve: it can suspend, revoke or reprimand a licence, but it cannot recover a penny for you.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Two years from the injury for personal injury, which includes assault, battery and negligence. Courts treat false imprisonment as a one-year claim.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For someone injured as a child, the same number of years (usually two) starts at 18. No claim can be brought more than 20 years after the injury. West Virginia's special longer deadline in this section is for childhood sexual abuse only.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: Suits against a county, city, school board or other political subdivision must be filed within two years of the injury (or of its discovery), and a child still gets the extra time until 18. Before suing a state agency, you must mail written notice to the agency head and the Attorney General at least 30 days in advance.
items.citation: W. Va. Code § 29-12A-6(a) (political subdivisions); W. Va. Code § 55-17-3(a) (state agencies)

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: No time limit for felony child abuse: West Virginia has no statute of limitations for felonies. Misdemeanor child abuse must be charged within one year.
items.citation: W. Va. Code § 61-11-9 (limits misdemeanors and perjury only); W. Va. Code § 61-8D-3 (child abuse)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: No time limit for felony malicious or unlawful wounding. Misdemeanor assault and battery must be charged within one year.
items.citation: W. Va. Code § 61-11-9; W. Va. Code § 61-2-9

channels.name: West Virginia Board of Examiners in Counseling
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses professional counselors and marriage and family therapists in West Virginia and enforces the licensure rules and ethical standards. On a finding of probable cause it can reprimand, suspend or revoke a licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It cannot seek or recover any money for the person who complained. Its meetings discussing complaints and investigations are confidential and closed to the public.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor or marriage and family therapist in West Virginia.
channels.how: Contact the Board to request a complaint form.
channels.mail: West Virginia Board of Examiners in Counseling, 815 Quarrier Street, Suite 212, Charleston, WV 25301

channels.name: West Virginia Board of Examiners of Psychologists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in West Virginia.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist.
channels.how: Use the Board's complaint page.

channels.name: West Virginia Centralized Intake for Abuse and Neglect
channels.what_it_can_do: The single point of entry for every report of suspected abuse and neglect in West Virginia, covering both children and vulnerable adults. Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
channels.who_to_report: A child under 18 at a West Virginia program who is being abused or neglected, or is at risk of it. Anyone concerned for a child can report.
channels.how: Call Centralized Intake, and report to local law enforcement as well. Mandated reporters may also send a non-emergency report by email.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year.

channels.name: West Virginia Department of Human Services, facility complaints
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates West Virginia's residential and behavioral health facilities and takes complaints about them. The state also maintains an abuse registry covering people barred from working in these settings.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed West Virginia facility.
channels.how: Contact the Department's complaint line, and report any abuse to Centralized Intake as well.

channels.name: Disability Rights of West Virginia
channels.what_it_can_do: West Virginia's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A West Virginia program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against all defendants is age 36 with a 4-year discovery rule and a revival law, reviving claims up to age 36.
criminal: CSA: There is no criminal SOL for any felonies, including CSA. The SOL for misdemeanors is 1 year from the offense.
Trafficking: There is no SOL for trafficking felonies.
CSAM: There is no SOL for CSAM felonies.

states.note: Wisconsin gives anyone receiving mental health or substance use treatment a statutory set of client rights, with a formal grievance procedure behind them and client rights staff who will write the grievance for you if you ask. That is separate from complaining about the clinician or the facility, and it is the channel most people in a Wisconsin program have never been told exists.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: Three years for assault, battery, false imprisonment and other intentional harm, and three years for negligence and other personal injury.
items.citation: Wis. Stat. § 893.57 (intentional torts); Wis. Stat. § 893.54(1m)(a) (injury to the person)

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For someone injured as a child, the deadline is the later of the normal three years from the injury or two years after turning 18, which is age 20. Wisconsin's longer deadline for childhood abuse (until age 35) covers sexual abuse only.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: For a county, city, school district or other local government, serve written notice within 120 days of the injury, and file an itemized claim. If the claim is denied, you have six months from the denial notice to sue. For a state employee, serve written notice on the Attorney General within 120 days of the injury.
items.citation: Wis. Stat. § 893.80(1d), (1g) (local governments); Wis. Stat. § 893.82(3) (state officers and employees)

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: Physical abuse of a child can be charged until the victim turns 45 if it caused great bodily harm on purpose. Other physical child abuse, reckless abuse, failing to protect a child, and causing a child mental harm can be charged until the victim turns 26. The normal six years from the offense applies if it ends later.
items.citation: Wis. Stat. § 939.74(2)(c), (2)(cm); Wis. Stat. § 948.03 (physical abuse of a child); § 948.04 (causing mental harm to a child)

items.label: Assault
items.summary: Six years from the offense for felony battery or assault. Misdemeanor battery: three years.

channels.name: Wisconsin Marriage and Family Therapy, Professional Counseling and Social Work Examining Board
channels.what_it_can_do: A combined board under the Department of Safety and Professional Services covering marriage and family therapists, professional counselors and social workers. DSPS provides the investigators and prosecutors for it, and the board disciplines the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed marriage and family therapist, professional counselor or social worker in Wisconsin. Psychologists have their own examining board under the same department.
channels.how: File a written complaint through the Department's Division of Legal Services and Compliance. Board staff first decide whether it is within their jurisdiction.
channels.note: Complaints are accepted from clients, employers, colleagues and other agencies alike.

channels.name: Wisconsin client rights grievance procedure (DHS 94)
channels.what_it_can_do: Wisconsin law gives people receiving mental health, substance use or developmental disability services a set of client rights and a formal grievance procedure to enforce them. The provider must have a client rights specialist, and a grievance can be escalated beyond the provider.
channels.who_to_report: Someone in a Wisconsin program whose rights are being breached - restrictions, treatment, how they are being handled day to day - whether or not it amounts to abuse.
channels.how: File a formal grievance using the sample form, or ask a client rights staff member to write it down for you, which the Department says they will do. There is a published flow chart of the whole procedure.

channels.name: Wisconsin DHS, residential and community-based care licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and certifies Wisconsin's residential and community-based care providers and takes complaints against them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed residential program.
channels.how: Use the Department's complaint route.

channels.name: Disability Rights Wisconsin
channels.what_it_can_do: Wisconsin's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy. The Department of Health Services names it directly as where to take a disability rights grievance.
channels.who_to_report: A Wisconsin program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

channels.name: Wisconsin county Child Protective Services
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a child protection response. Wisconsin's CPS is state-supervised but county-administered in 71 counties, and state-administered in Milwaukee, so the report goes to the county agency where the child is. An Access worker takes it and decides whether it meets the statutory definition.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Wisconsin program. Anyone can report, to the local CPS agency or to law enforcement.
channels.how: Find the county agency in the Department's directory and call it; the directory also lists after-hours numbers. If the abuse is happening now or is violent, call 911.

civil: CSA: The civil SOL for CSA claims against perpetrators is age 35. The SOL against other types of defendants is age 20, with a narrow exception for negligent supervision claims against religious organizations for clergy abuse, which have an SOL of age 35.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking claims is age 20.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM claims is age 20.
criminal: CSA: There is no SOL for some first-degree CSA felonies, an SOL of age 45 for other CSA felonies, and 3 years from the offense for misdemeanors.
Trafficking: The SOL for trafficking is age 45.
CSAM: The SOL for CSAM violations is age 45.

states.note: Wyoming reports abuse to the county field office where it happened rather than to a statewide hotline, with 911 as the around-the-clock route. It also has a Department of Family Services ombudsman who takes complaints about the Department's own handling of a case, which is the escalation route when a report goes nowhere.

items.label: Physical abuse or injury
items.summary: One year for assault, battery and false imprisonment. Four years for negligence and other personal injury.

items.label: If it happened before you turned 18
items.summary: For someone injured as a child, the deadline is three years after turning 18 (age 21), or the normal period if that ends later. Wyoming has no longer deadline for physical abuse of a child. Its special rule in § 1-3-105(b) covers sexual assault only.

items.label: If the program was run by or for the government
items.summary: To sue the state or a local government, first present a written, itemized claim within two years of the act (or two years after discovery, in limited cases). You must then file the lawsuit within one year after filing the claim.

items.label: Physical child abuse
items.summary: No time limit. Wyoming has no statute of limitations for any crime, so child abuse can be charged at any time.
items.citation: No criminal statute of limitations in Wyoming; Ridinger v. State, 2021 WY 4, ¶ 14, 478 P.3d 1160 (quoting Phillips v. State, 835 P.2d 1062, 1069 (Wyo. 1992))

items.label: Assault
items.summary: No time limit. Aggravated assault, and misdemeanor assault and battery, can be charged at any time.

channels.name: Wyoming Mental Health Professions Licensing Board
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines Wyoming's counselors, certified alcohol and drug abuse counselors and certified mental health workers. Anyone may complain - clients and former clients, family members, colleagues and co-workers all do.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: Complaints can only be filed against individuals, not against a practice or a program.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed or certified mental health professional in Wyoming.
channels.how: File through the Board's complaints page. A copy of your complaint goes to the licence or certificate holder.
channels.note: The Board says the review, investigation and legal stages may take a long time, depending on the complexity of the case and the caseload already waiting.

channels.name: Wyoming Board of Psychology
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in Wyoming.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist.
channels.how: File through the Board's public page.

channels.name: Wyoming child abuse and neglect reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a Department of Family Services child protection response. Reports go to the county field office where the abuse or neglect happened or is happening.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Wyoming program. Report to the county the program sits in.
channels.how: Call the county field office, or 911 at any hour to reach local law enforcement. The state line will also direct you.
channels.phone_note: Also 307-777-7564. For an emergency at any hour, 911.

channels.name: Wyoming DFS child care and facility licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses Wyoming's child care and residential facilities and takes concerns that one has breached its licensing requirements.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Wyoming facility.
channels.how: Contact the child care licenser for the area, or the licensing support contact.

channels.name: Wyoming DFS Ombudsman
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints about how the Department of Family Services has handled a case.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It reviews the Department rather than the program.
channels.who_to_report: A family or young person whose report to DFS has gone nowhere.

channels.name: Wyoming Protection and Advocacy System
channels.what_it_can_do: Wyoming's federally mandated P&A, with authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Wyoming program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.how: Contact the intake line.

civil: The civil SOL for CSA, trafficking, and CSAM claims against all defendants is age 26 with a 3-year discovery rule.
criminal: There is no SOL for any felonies or misdemeanors, including CSA, trafficking, and CSAM offenses.
